import sys, json, uuid, datetime, re, collections

# The incoming message and this cell's own configuration arrive on the same
# stdin document, so it is read before the first knob rather than after the
# prompt text below; `d`, `envelope` and the rest of the message are unpacked
# where they always were.
doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
# This cell's OWN configuration arrives on the same stdin document: `params` is
# one of its three top-level objects, beside `envelope` and `body`, and the
# substrate always sets it ({} when there is nothing to hand over). Every knob
# below is read from it, so each one is per-INSTANCE configuration -- two
# members of one colony have their memories tuned apart, and a mutation retunes
# one of them without touching a colony-wide environment (GH #138). The literal
# beside each name is the shipped default; it is the same value the template
# config and `contract.settings` carry, and a test pins the three against each
# other.
P = doc.get("params") or {}


def _knob(key, default):
    # A knob explicitly set to NULL is "not configured", not a crash: an
    # operator who blanks a line in a config means the default. WHITESPACE is
    # decided one level down, by the accessor, because the two classes want
    # opposite things: `_int`/`_float` fall back on a blank string (there is no
    # number in it), while `_str` keeps it, because for a name knob the empty
    # string is a VALUE -- it is how `self_legacy_subject` is switched off.
    v = P.get(key, default)
    return default if v is None else v


def _int(key, default):
    v = _knob(key, default)
    if isinstance(v, str) and not v.strip():
        return default
    return int(v)


def _float(key, default):
    v = _knob(key, default)
    if isinstance(v, str) and not v.strip():
        return default
    return float(v)


def _str(key, default):
    v = _knob(key, default)
    return "" if v is None else str(v)


# GH #1040: a knob the MODEL PACKAGE sizes. The bundle and the query limits
# below were fixed numbers from the time of 32k windows: a bundle of 2000
# tokens is about 2 % of what the answering model can use today (KD2 § 3,
# talky at 11-35k prompt tokens under a 120k cap). Shipped as null, such a
# knob is DERIVED per request from the asker's `input_soft` (the llm cell's
# stamp since GH #1037, handed over by the curator's ask as
# `recall_input_soft`, see `package_limits`); a number is an override that
# wins over the package. The literal beside the name is the value without a
# package -- an ask that names none sizes the bundle exactly as before.
_PKG_FALLBACK = {}
_PKG_SET = {}


def _pkg(key, fallback):
    _PKG_FALLBACK[key] = fallback
    v = _knob(key, None)
    if v is None or (isinstance(v, str) and not v.strip()):
        _PKG_SET[key] = None
    else:
        _PKG_SET[key] = int(v)
    return _PKG_SET[key]

# The keyword leg's stop words are language DATA with one home: the files
# beside the cell (`recall/lang/<code>.json`, key `stopwords`), copied byte for
# byte into `params.stopwords_lang` and its declared default. Every language is
# applied at once -- a query is filtered against the union -- and a language is
# added by a file, never by script text. A malformed or absent knob filters
# nothing (the leg keeps every token it would otherwise have dropped).
def _stop_words(langs):
    out = set()
    if isinstance(langs, dict):
        for block in langs.values():
            words = block.get("stopwords") if isinstance(block, dict) else None
            if isinstance(words, str):
                out.update(words.split())
    return out

# ------------------------------------------------- QUERY HYGIENE GUARD (GH #88)
# The recall lane's only defence against an UNBOUNDED CONSUMER -- a caller whose
# tool-call query is not a question but a question with its whole preamble glued
# in front of it. Such a query poisons BOTH tier-1 legs at once: the semantic leg

#

# before the leg fan, the same place a half-open window is rejected (R5) and for
# the same reason: a bad request must not cost a full tier-1 fan-out first.

# >>> content-budget v1 (R-IG-1, GH #1085)
CHARS_PER_TOKEN = 3


def budget_chars(input_soft, share):
    """Characters a producer may hand a model whose usable window is
    `input_soft` tokens (the catalog row, cut by the curator), for a section
    that takes `share` of that window. None when no window is known: the
    producer then delivers its content whole."""
    try:
        soft = int(float(input_soft))
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None
    if soft <= 0:
        return None
    return int(soft * share * CHARS_PER_TOKEN)


def clip(text, limit, hint="budget of the window"):
    """`text` whole when it fits `limit` (None: no limit); else its head and
    a mark naming what was shown, the total and how to get the rest."""
    text = "" if text is None else str(text)
    if limit is None or len(text) <= limit:
        return text
    limit = max(0, int(limit))
    return text[:limit] + "...[cut: %d of %d chars shown; %s]" % (
        limit, len(text), hint)
# <<< content-budget v1


# >>> token-estimate v1 (GH #1098)
# The one token estimate of the templates: a request as the llm cell
# estimates it before it refuses one over `input_hard` (`window.rs`
# `estimate_prompt_tokens`) for a model whose catalogue row states no rates
# of its own -- UTF-8 bytes of every string and object key, 4 for a number
# or a bool, over CHARS_PER_TOKEN of the content-budget block (the same
# three bytes a token every budget of the templates is sized with), rounded
# up; a string starting `data:` (an inline image) counts IMAGE_TOKENS, the
# cell's own `llm::window::IMAGE_TOKENS`.
IMAGE_TOKENS = 1024


def estimate_tokens(value):
    """Tokens of `value` (any JSON value) by the rule above."""
    nbytes, images, todo = 0, 0, [value]
    while todo:
        v = todo.pop()
        if isinstance(v, str):
            if v.startswith("data:"):
                images += 1
            else:
                nbytes += len(v.encode("utf-8"))
        elif isinstance(v, dict):
            for k, x in v.items():
                nbytes += len(str(k).encode("utf-8"))
                todo.append(x)
        elif isinstance(v, (list, tuple)):
            todo.extend(v)
        elif isinstance(v, (bool, int, float)):
            nbytes += 4
    return tokens_of_bytes(nbytes) + images * IMAGE_TOKENS


def tokens_of_bytes(nbytes):
    """Tokens of `nbytes` bytes (or characters) of text: over
    CHARS_PER_TOKEN, rounded up."""
    return -(-max(0, int(nbytes)) // CHARS_PER_TOKEN)
# <<< token-estimate v1

def asked_soft(ctx):

            return v
    return None


def fit_text(item, key, room, cost):
    """`item` with `item[key]` cut -- with its mark -- to the longest head for
    which `cost(item)` stays within `room` tokens; None when not even the mark
    fits. R-IG-1: the one place an item of a bundle is ever cut."""
    text = str(item.get(key) or "")
    lo, hi, best = 0, len(text), None
    while lo <= hi:
        mid = (lo + hi) // 2
        trial = dict(item)
        trial[key] = clip(text, mid, CUT_HINT)
        if cost(trial) <= room:
            best, lo = trial, mid + 1
        else:
            hi = mid - 1
    return best

SENTENCE_END = re.compile(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+")


def sanitize_query(text):
    """The query the legs actually see, plus the verdict that says so (#88).

    Three steps, in this order, and only above QUERY_SAFE_CHARS:

      1. `question`      -- the LAST sentence ending in `?`. A contaminated
                            query carries its question at the end, which is the
                            half the old head-cap threw away;
      2. `tail-sentence` -- no question mark anywhere: the last sentence;
      3. `truncate`      -- what survived is STILL too long (a blob without a
                            single sentence end is the unbounded consumer in its
                            purest form): the last QUERY_MAX_CHARS characters.
                            The cut is by character and may split a word --
                            deterministic beats clever, and the keyword leg drops
                            sub-3-char tokens anyway.

    Step 3 is a clamp, not merely a fallback, so the effective query is bounded
    for EVERY input. That bound is the whole point: the cost of a recall stops
    depending on how much context the caller pasted.

    Returns (query, verdict). The verdict is None exactly when nothing was
    applied, and that is what keeps a healthy query byte-identical -- no field,
    no header key, no rendered line, nothing.

    NOT a reject. A half-open window is a caller BUG (R5); a contaminated query
    is not -- the session-boot request of spec D.1 carries no query at all and
    must still answer, and the collector sends the slot on every hop. The guard
    clamps and SAYS SO; it never refuses, and it never scans silently.
    """
    raw = str(text or "")
    if len(raw) <= QUERY_SAFE_CHARS:
        return raw, None
    parts = [p.strip() for p in SENTENCE_END.split(raw) if p.strip()]
    questions = [p for p in parts if p.endswith("?")]
    if questions:
        step, kept = "question", questions[-1]
    elif parts:
        step, kept = "tail-sentence", parts[-1]
    else:
        step, kept = "truncate", raw
    if len(kept) > QUERY_MAX_CHARS:
        step, kept = "truncate", kept[-QUERY_MAX_CHARS:]
    return kept, {"step": step, "from_chars": len(raw), "to_chars": len(kept)}

# ------------------------------------------------------- AUDIENCE GATE (#244)
# ADR-0002 E11/E12 and the 0.16.0 contract: every row that leaves this read path
# is measured against the round that is asking. The gate is a PREDICATE ON
# CANDIDATES, never a filter on rendered output -- a hidden row must not reach
# the RRF sum (it would move the ranking of the visible ones) and must not spend
# a byte of the tier-0 token budget that a visible row could have used.
#
# Four row kinds carry the tags (contract, Nachtrag 1): `episodes` and `facts`
# (channel + audience_set), `entity_edges` (inherited from their episode, and
# they ARE the graph leg) and `beliefs` (audience_set only -- a belief is
# DERIVED, it was never said in a room, so the third clause below can never fire
# for one and the subset rule alone decides). `entities` deliberately carries no
# tag: an entity is only ever reached over an edge or a fact, and those are
# filtered.
def audience_of(value):
    """A participant set off the store: a JSON list in a text column. Anything
    that is not a JSON list reads as the EMPTY set, which is invisible to every
    non-empty round -- unreadable provenance is not a licence."""
    if isinstance(value, list):
        items = value
    else:
        try:
            items = json.loads(value or "[]")
        except Exception:
            return set()
    if not isinstance(items, list):
        return set()
    return {str(i) for i in items}


def read_audience_now(ctx):
    """The asking round, off `context.audience_now` (a JSON list the port edge
    promotes). None means "no audience given" and becomes a REJECT, never an
    empty set: the empty set is a subset of everything and would open the whole
    hive. An empty LIST is treated the same way, for exactly that reason."""
    raw = ctx.get("audience_now")
    if raw is None:
        return None
    if not isinstance(raw, list) and not str(raw).strip():
        return None
    got = audience_of(raw)
    return got or None

def visible(row_audience_set, row_channel):
    """The rule, verbatim from the 0.16.0 audience-gate contract (GH #244).

    Universal release wins. Otherwise the CURRENT round must be a SUBSET of the
    round the row was recorded in -- the same subset rule `affinity/brief`
    already decides disclosures with, so the two gates speak one language.
    The third clause is the channel-local exception of ADR-0002 E11 and NEVER
    crosses a channel boundary: `row_channel == now_channel` is a condition, not
    a courtesy, so the dangerous direction (private 1:1 -> group channel) stays
    shut in every case. A row without an `audience_set` is INVISIBLE, not
    visible, and it is refused FIRST (R2 below): no non-empty round is a subset
    of the empty set, and no other clause may hand it a way round that.
    """
    aud = audience_of(row_audience_set)
    # R2 (Nachtrag 2), and the ORDER is normative: a row with no participant set
    # is refused BEFORE the channel clause is even reached. The open-history
    # clause is a relaxation for rows whose provenance we HAVE -- "the room
    # already showed it" -- never a rescue for a row whose provenance is
    # missing, because for such a row we do not know whether the room showed it.
    # Without this line the weakest data path would be the most permissive one:
    # the one row we know nothing about would be the one that gets through.
    if not aud:
        return False
    if "*" in aud:
        return True
    # `audience_now is None` cannot happen on a fresh request (it was rejected
    # at the entry), only on a store reply whose context lost the key. Then the
    # subset clause is skipped rather than evaluated against nothing, which
    # keeps the failure closed instead of opening it.
    if audience_now is None:
        # The round is unknown: this can only happen on a store reply whose
        # context lost the key (a fresh request without it was rejected at the
        # entry). Then NOTHING is visible -- not even through the channel
        # clause. "The room already showed it" presumes the asker is in the
        # room, and without a round we cannot know that. An unknown round is
        # refused, never accommodated.
        return False
    if audience_now <= aud:
        return True
    if open_history and row_channel and str(row_channel) == now_channel:
        return True
    return False

# audit -- and leaves every answer here, on the one gate every leg already

# it. close-glue MUTES what a request names (`muted_at`, `mute_source`
# `forget_request:<turn>`, `mute_words`; `unmuted_at` once the member takes the
# topic up again) instead of closing it -- the `forget_request:` closures above
# are what a store of the closing releases still holds until its first close
# pass converts them. A muted row is never RAISED: the tier-0 bundle (built per
# turn, no question asked) and every ask whose words do not name the topic leave
# it out, the same gate, before any rank or budget. It ANSWERS a direct
# question: an ask whose words carry every one of the row's `mute_words` (the
# member's "what did my neighbour owe me again?", or the model's
# `memory_recall` naming it) gets it like any other row. The mode is the
# asker's words, not a knob: recall cannot tell a question from a turn, but it
# can tell an ask that names the muted thing from one that does not, and a
# caller cannot forget to set it. A mute without words answers every ask with
# words of the asker (kfm M1c, review 4: never muted AND unanswerable).
def muted(row):

            and not str(row.get("unmuted_at") or "").strip())

# `compose`). That prefix is the push's guess at what the conversation is
# about -- the open topic comes from the model's own memory section, written
# by a model that never saw the muted row -- not the asker naming the topic.
# Counted, an open topic whose name carries every word of a mute would raise
# the muted row on an ambient turn (kfm M1, open point of OR-kfm.M1.2). So
# only the words after the prefix count, and of those only the ones the query
# guard kept (`query`, GH #88).
PUSH_PREFIX = re.compile(r"\A\[(?:topic|mentioned|refers to): .*?\] ", re.S)

def names_word(word, asked):
    """Whether a set of asked words carries one word of a mute: the word
    itself or the same word inflected. The request said "owes", the question
    says "owe"; "neighbours". kfm M1c (review 3): two words are one
    where they share a prefix of max(4, the shorter one less two) letters
    ("repaid" / "repaying"; "owed" / "owing" no), a short word of five
    letters or fewer all of it but its last ("owed" / "owes", "owe" / "owes"),
    and never fewer than three ("own" is no "owe"). Deterministic and blind
    to the language."""
    if word in asked:
        return True
    for a in asked:
        short = min(len(a), len(word))
        need = max(3, short - 1) if short <= 5 else max(4, short - 2)
        common = 0
        for x, y in zip(a, word):
            if x != y:
                break
            common += 1
        if common >= need:
            return True
    return False


def asked_for(row, asked=None):
    """Whether this ask (or the words `asked`) names a muted row's topic.

    kfm M1c (review 3): every word of it, or -- where the asker's own words
    are a QUESTION (a `?` after the push prefix) -- all of them but one, and
    at least one: "How much does my neighbour still owe me?" asks about
    "money neighbour owes", "What did the doctor say?" about "ann doctor". A
    statement that names part of a topic ("My neighbour waved at me") raises
    nothing, and tier 0 asks with no words at all, so it never does.
    Review 4: a mute without words answers every ask with words of the asker
    and still none on tier 0 -- muted, never unanswerable."""
    words = set(str(row.get("mute_words") or "").split())
    have = ASKED_WORDS if asked is None else asked
    if not words:
        return bool(have)
    hits = sum(1 for w in words if names_word(w, have))
    if hits == len(words):
        return True
    question = (asked is None and phase != "legs"
                and "?" in PUSH_PREFIX.sub("", str(ctx.get("recall_query", "")), count=1))
    return question and hits >= max(1, len(words) - 1)

    third clause false all by itself -- the conservative reading, and the
    intended one. A forgotten row is visible to nobody (GH #1039); a muted one
    only to an ask that names it (R-TR-25)."""

# ------------------------------------------------------ AFFECT MARK (GH #936)
# An episode may carry a mark of how its turn read (`episodes.affect`, written
# through the hive's `in_affect` lane by a recognizer elsewhere in the colony).
# Recall hands it back with every candidate and may be asked to keep only
# candidates whose mark lies inside a filter. It is never a ranking signal:
# what the mark MEANS is the asker's business, and a memory that re-ordered its
# answer by mood would bend every reader's view the same way.
#
# The filter runs on candidates that already passed the audience gate -- it
# narrows what a round may see, it never widens it.
AFFECT_FILTER_KEYS = {"valence_max": (-1, 1), "valence_min": (-1, 1),
                      "arousal_min": (0, 1), "min_confidence": (0, 1)}


def parse_affect_filter(raw):
    """`hop.affect_filter` (a JSON object as text, promoted to context by the
    hive's door) -> (filter, None), (None, None) when unset, or (None, <key>)
    naming what is wrong. `{}` is a filter: it keeps marked candidates only."""
    if raw is None or (isinstance(raw, str) and not raw.strip()):
        return None, None
    try:
        f = json.loads(raw) if isinstance(raw, str) else raw
    except Exception:
        return None, "affect_filter"
    if not isinstance(f, dict):
        return None, "affect_filter"
    for k in sorted(f):
        if k not in AFFECT_FILTER_KEYS:
            return None, k
        v = f[k]
        lo, hi = AFFECT_FILTER_KEYS[k]
        if isinstance(v, bool) or not isinstance(v, (int, float)) or not (lo <= v <= hi):
            return None, k
    return f, None


def parse_mark(raw):
    """A stored mark (text column) as a dict, or None for unknown. A mark that
    does not read as one is unknown -- never a guessed reading."""
    try:
        m = json.loads(raw) if isinstance(raw, str) else raw
    except Exception:
        return None
    if not isinstance(m, dict):
        return None
    for k in ("valence", "arousal", "confidence"):
        if isinstance(m.get(k), bool) or not isinstance(m.get(k), (int, float)):
            return None
    return m


def affect_pass(f, mark):
    """True when no filter is set, or the mark lies inside it. A candidate
    without a mark never passes a set filter: unknown is not inside anything."""
    if f is None:
        return True
    if mark is None:
        return False
    if "valence_max" in f and mark["valence"] > f["valence_max"]:
        return False
    if "valence_min" in f and mark["valence"] < f["valence_min"]:
        return False
    if "arousal_min" in f and mark["arousal"] < f["arousal_min"]:
        return False
    if "min_confidence" in f and mark["confidence"] < f["min_confidence"]:
        return False
    return True

# sees an error here treats the filter as unset rather than guessing a bound.
affect_filter, affect_filter_err = parse_affect_filter(ctx.get("affect_filter"))

def payloads_by_id(doc):
    """One entry per leg of a BUNDLE reply, keyed by its `tool_call_id` (#295).

    A bundle answers N ops with TWO arrays that mean one thing. `messages[]`
    carries the `tool_result` turns in call order and nothing else: the turn
    schema (`$defs/TurnObject`) is closed, so a turn cannot carry its own
    metadata and a reply that tried would be dead-lettered whole. The body's
    top-level `results[]` carries what a single-op reply puts on the hop --
    `operation`, `rows_affected`, `duration_ms` and, for a refused leg,
    `error_code`. `tool_call_id` joins the two halves, and this reads both so
    that nothing downstream has to know there were two.
    """
    out = {}
    for m in doc.get("messages") or []:
        if not isinstance(m, dict):
            continue
        try:
            payload = json.loads(m.get("text") or "")
        except Exception:
            payload = None
        out[str(m.get("id") or "")] = {"payload": payload, "operation": "", "error_code": ""}
    for r in doc.get("results") or []:
        if not isinstance(r, dict):
            continue
        leg = out.setdefault(str(r.get("tool_call_id") or ""),
                             {"payload": None, "operation": "", "error_code": ""})
        leg["operation"] = str(r.get("operation") or "")
        leg["error_code"] = str(r.get("error_code") or "")
    return out

    right for every op but `traverse`: that one answers a document

def store_bundle(calls, ph):
    """GH #295 -- N ops in ONE message, answered in ONE reply.

    `calls` is [(tool_call_id, args), ...] in the order the ops should run. The
    store runs them sequentially over its one connection and answers with one
    `tool_result` turn plus one `results[]` entry per call, correlated by that
    id -- which is why the ids are given here rather than derived from the
    phase: one message, one phase, N ops.
    """
    return {"header": {"route": "rstore", "phase": ph, "recall_id": rid},
            "messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call", "id": cid,
                          "text": json.dumps(args)} for cid, args in calls]}



def park_and_read(rows, ph, legs=None):
    """GH #418 -- park what this hop computed AND read the request's parking
    place back, in ONE message.

    The `store` is a stateful cell: one task, one connection, one message at a
    time (`docs/cell-types.md`, Concurrency note). A bundle is one message, so
    its ops run in order against a database nobody else is writing to in the
    meantime -- the trailing select therefore sees the inserts in front of it,
    and of two hops that park concurrently exactly ONE reads a complete set,
    because the other one's insert had not happened when its own select ran.

    That is precisely what `update ... set fired=1 where fired=0` plus
    `rows_affected` used to buy, and it costs no message of its own. The three
    guard rows of the tier-1 path go with the three gates that used them.
    """
    calls = [("r-" + ph + "-" + leg,
              {"operation": "insert", "table": "recall_scratch",
               "row": {"request_id": rid, "leg": leg, "payload": json.dumps(payload),
                       "created_at": now, "fired": 0}})
             for leg, payload in rows]
    where = {"request_id": rid}
    if legs:
        where["leg"] = {"in": list(legs)}
    calls.append(("r-" + ph + "-read",
                  {"operation": "select", "table": "recall_scratch",
                   "columns": ["request_id", "leg", "payload", "fired"],
                   "where": where}))
    return store_bundle(calls, ph)


def legs_from(rows):
    """Decode a page of `recall_scratch` rows into `(legs, worst)`.

    `worst` is the highest number of rows any ONE leg arrived with. `worst > 1`
    is a redelivery, not a complete set: reading it as complete would emit the
    bundle twice, so the caller parks on it. This is the exactly-once half the
    guarded update also carried, kept explicit rather than inherited.
    """
    out, seen = {}, collections.Counter()
    for r in rows:
        if not isinstance(r, dict):
            continue
        leg = str(r.get("leg") or "")
        seen[leg] += 1
        try:
            out[leg] = json.loads(r.get("payload") or "[]")
        except Exception:
            out[leg] = []
    return out, (max(seen.values()) if seen else 0)


def parked(doc, ph):
    """The parking place as the trailing select of `park_and_read` answered it."""
    return legs_from(bundle_rows(payloads_by_id(doc), "r-" + ph + "-read"))


def scratch_insert(leg, payload, ph="t1-collect"):
    return store_op({"operation": "insert", "table": "recall_scratch",
                     "row": {"request_id": rid, "leg": leg, "payload": json.dumps(payload),
                             "created_at": now, "fired": 0}}, ph)


def leg_payload(hits, page_rows, limit):
    """A leg's scratch payload: its rank list plus the LIMIT its page came back on.

    #280 (item 3): whether a page was capped is knowable only WHERE THE PAGE
    ARRIVED. Summing the gated leg sizes at the end answers a different question
    and gets it wrong in both directions: the keyword leg is two sub-searches
    with a limit each, so 12 + 8 = 20 reports a cap that never fired, and the
    semantic leg is counted AFTER its audience gate, so a full page that loses
    three rows to the gate counts 17 and reports nothing. Hence `page_rows` is
    the PRE-GATE row count of the page this leg was handed, never the length of
    what survived it.

    A page that came back SHORT writes exactly what a leg has always written --
    its rank list and nothing else -- so every consumer of an uncapped leg reads
    the shape it has always read (#244 pins the leg payloads as rank lists, and
    an uncapped leg is the overwhelming majority of them). Only a FULL page wraps
    the list, because only a full page has something more to say. The wrapper is
    the exception, never the new normal.

    A page that is exactly full counts as capped: the store answers with rows,
    not with "and there are more", so an exactly-full page is genuinely ambiguous
    and the conservative reading is the one that does not claim a completeness it
    cannot have.
    """
    if page_rows < limit:
        return hits
    return {"hits": hits, "capped_at": limit}


def leg_hits(payload):
    """The rank list of a leg payload -- bare list (never near a limit) or dict."""
    if isinstance(payload, dict):
        return payload.get("hits") or []
    return payload if isinstance(payload, list) else []


def leg_cap(payload):
    """The limit this leg's page came back on, 0 when it came back short."""
    if isinstance(payload, dict):
        try:
            return int(payload.get("capped_at") or 0)
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            return 0
    return 0


def raw_size(payload):
    """The pre-floor row count a bookkeeping leg carries (#297).

    Zero for anything else, so a request that predates these legs -- or one whose
    keyword phase never ran because the query held no usable token -- fuses with
    a raw size of 0, which is exactly what it means.
    """
    if isinstance(payload, dict):
        try:
            return int(payload.get("n") or 0)
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            return 0
    return 0


def scratch_select(ph, legs=None):
    where = {"request_id": rid}
    if legs:
        where["leg"] = {"in": list(legs)}
    return store_op({"operation": "select", "table": "recall_scratch",
                     "columns": ["request_id", "leg", "payload", "fired"], "where": where}, ph)


def scratch_guard(leg, ph):
    """The exactly-once gate: whoever's guarded update reports rows_affected > 0
    owns the next step. One guard ROW per gate, so the three gates of a tier-1
    request never steal each other's flag."""
    return store_op({"operation": "update", "table": "recall_scratch", "set": {"fired": 1},
                     "where": {"request_id": rid, "leg": leg, "fired": 0}}, ph)


def by_leg(doc):
    out = {}
    for r in rows_of(doc):
        try:
            out[r.get("leg")] = json.loads(r.get("payload") or "[]")
        except Exception:
            out[r.get("leg")] = []
    return out


def holder_of():
    if ctx.get("memory_holder"):
        return str(ctx["memory_holder"])
    if ctx.get("user_id"):
        return "user:" + str(ctx["user_id"])
    return "self"


# ------------------------------------------- THE ASKER IS AN ANCHOR (GH #536)
def self_names():
    """The names of whoever is ASKING, out of the context the request carries.

    A question in the first person -- "what are my sons called?" -- names
    nobody. The graph anchors are built from the query text and from the
    subjects of the keyword hits, so such a question resolves its own
    interrogative words against `entities` (measured live: `in ["Heissen",
    "Meine", "Soehne", ...] -> []`), the walk never starts, and the entity the
    question is actually ABOUT never enters the retrieval at all.

    The asker was never missing from the request. `audience_now` carries the
    participant set in affinity vocabulary, and the `member:` tokens in it are
    people; the read path just never read it as an IDENTITY, only as the
    audience gate's yardstick. So the identity is taken where it already stands
    rather than added as a key nobody promotes.

    Three sources, most explicit first: `memory_holder`, the `user_id` a caller
    stamps, and the `member:`/`person:` tokens of the asking round. `agent:` is
    deliberately not one of them -- the hive belongs to a MEMBER (ADR-0002 E1)
    and the agent is a lens on it, so an agent's own name must not pull the
    member's dossier under a second identity.

    Nothing here widens what a round may SEE. Every row an anchor reaches is
    still measured against `audience_now` by the same gate as every other row:
    an anchor decides what is LOOKED UP, never what is disclosed.
    """
    raw = []
    for value in (ctx.get("memory_holder"), ctx.get("user_id")):
        text = str(value or "").strip()
        if text:
            raw.append(text.split(":")[-1])
    for token in sorted(audience_now or ()):
        kind, _, local = str(token).partition(":")
        if kind in ("member", "person") and local.strip():
            raw.append(local.strip())
    if SELF_LEGACY_SUBJECT:
        raw.append(SELF_LEGACY_SUBJECT)
    out = []
    for name in raw:
        # Case variants for the same reason the query anchors carry them: the
        # store's `in` is exact, `entities.canonical_name` keeps the written
        # spelling and an audience token is lower-cased by convention.
        for variant in (name, name.lower(), name.capitalize()):
            if variant and variant not in out:
                out.append(variant)
    return out


def self_subjects():
    """The asker's names in `facts.canonical_subject` normalisation (GH #536).

    The same fold `node_key` performs for a walk node, written out rather than
    called: this runs at REQUEST ENTRY and `node_key` is defined further down,
    past the phase blocks. `facts.canonical_subject` is consistently lower-cased
    and the store's `in` filter is exact, so the fold has to happen on this side
    of the wire either way.
    """
    out = []
    for name in self_names():
        key = str(name or "").strip().lower()
        if key and key not in out:
            out.append(key)
    return out


def is_open(value):
    return value is None or value == ""


# GH #1057: the graph leg over the produced entity graph. Three things the
# walk needs since `entities`/`entity_edges` have a producer again (measured on
# a 6-month history, 27 entities, 256 edges, 10 of 20 two-hop questions wrong
# because the second person's current value never reached the bundle):
#   * NAME anchors. A person is a NAME of two or more words ("Frieda
#     Quastberg"), and the query tokens are single words, so the exact match
#     against `entities` never fired. The query's word runs and the name runs
#     of the keyword hits' claims are anchors as well.
#   * NODE rank. A node reached from several anchors, or that is an anchor
#     itself, is where the question's parts meet -- it goes first.
#   * FACT rank inside a node: the facts that share a word stem with the
#     question first, then the newest, at most GRAPH_NODE_FACTS of them, so a
#     node with fifteen facts cannot take every seat of the leg.
NAME_RUN = re.compile(r"[^\W\d_][\w'’-]*(?:\s+[^\W\d_][\w'’-]*)+")
CAP_RUN = re.compile(r"(?:(?<=\s)|^)([A-ZÀ-Þ][\w'’-]+(?:\s+[A-ZÀ-Þ][\w'’-]+)+)")


def name_anchors(text, claims):
    """Multi-word anchors: word runs of the query, capitalised runs of claims."""
    out = set()
    toks = [t for t in re.split(r"[^\w-]+", str(text or ""), flags=re.UNICODE) if t]
    for n in (2, 3):
        for i in range(len(toks) - n + 1):
            g = " ".join(toks[i:i + n])
            out.update([g, g.lower()])
    for c in claims:
        for m in CAP_RUN.finditer(str(c or "")):
            g = re.sub(r"['’]s$", "", m.group(1))
            words = g.split()
            for i in range(len(words)):
                for j in range(i + 2, min(len(words), i + 3) + 1):
                    w = " ".join(words[i:j])
                    out.update([w, w.lower()])
    return out


def stems(text):
    # `[\W_]`: a predicate is snake_case (`has_pet`), and "pet" must meet it.
    return {t.lower()[:4] for t in re.split(r"[\W_]+", str(text or ""), flags=re.UNICODE)
            if len(t) >= 3 and t.lower() not in STOP}


# GH #1057 (K2-M, kern2 fix round 3): a NAME is never evidence that a row is
# about the question. A rumour restates the name it is about ("Peer x said they
# heard Rufus Rietdorf moved to Rostock") and so does an old user statement
# ("Rufus Rietdorf lives in Lyon"), while the person's own current statement
# says "they" ("Peer y stated that they still live in Krakow"). Counting the
# name's stems ranked the rumour and the old value before the current one and
# cut the current one off the node page (measured, K2-M stale_vs_current-73/74:
# Krakow at seat 6 of the node, cap 3). "peer" is the reference prefix every
# peer statement carries.
PEER_STEMS = frozenset(["peer"])
# "now" asks for the current value; it is no content word. Measured (K2-M
# stale_vs_current-62): "quit being a baker and now works as a librarian" took a
# graph seat for "What car does Henrik Falkner drive now?".
TIME_STEMS = frozenset(["now"])


def name_stems(names):
    """Stems of entity names (walk node keys): never question words for a walk row."""
    out = set(PEER_STEMS)
    for n in names or ():
        out |= stems(n)
    return out


def walk_words(text, names):
    """The question's word stems a walk row may be matched on: names and time out."""
    return stems(text) - name_stems(names) - TIME_STEMS


def hearsay(row):
    """A fact somebody passed on about somebody else (rumour, relay, peer report).

    `source` names the participant who SAID it; a peer's own statement is filed
    under `peer <source>` (extract-glue `peer_subject`, see `named_ref`), and a
    statement of the member carries no source. Everything else is second hand.
    A row without the column (a page from before this fix) reads first-hand."""
    source = str(row.get("source") or "").strip().lower()
    if not source:
        return False
    return " ".join(str(row.get("subject") or "").lower().split()) != "peer " + source


def rank_walk(paths, anchor_rank, text=""):
    """Walk rows ranked by where the question's parts meet.

    A node scores 1/(1+r) for every distinct anchor that reaches it and once
    more when it is an anchor itself, r being the anchor's rank -- 0 for a
    name the question spells, i+1 for a name off the i-th keyword hit. So a
    node two strong anchors meet in outranks one a weak hit happened to touch.
    Before all of it: how many word stems of the question the RELATION of
    the edge into the node shares (`entity_edges.relation`, the claim that
    evidences it). "the flatmate of my nephew" walks the edge whose claim
    says flatmates first, not the one a rumour about a move left behind.
    Ties: depth, then accumulated weight, then the node.
    """
    # Names out (fix round 3): an edge whose claim merely spells a walked name
    # is no edge the question asked for.
    q = walk_words(text, [n for r in paths for n in (r.get("path") or [])])
    rel = {}
    for r in paths:
        node = str(r.get("node") or "").strip().lower()
        n = len(q & stems((r.get("edge") or {}).get("relation") or ""))
        rel[node] = max(rel.get(node, 0), n)
    def w(k):
        r = anchor_rank.get(k)
        return 0.0 if r is None else 1.0 / (1 + r)
    starts = {}
    for r in paths:
        path = r.get("path") or []
        node = str(r.get("node") or "").strip().lower()
        if path and int(r.get("depth", 0) or 0) >= 1:
            starts.setdefault(node, set()).add(str(path[0]).strip().lower())
    def meet(n):
        k = n.strip().lower()
        return sum(w(s) for s in starts.get(k, ())) + w(k)
    return sorted(paths, key=lambda r: (-rel.get(str(r.get("node") or "").strip().lower(), 0),
                                        -meet(str(r.get("node") or "")),
                                        int(r.get("depth", 99) or 99),
                                        -int(r.get("weight_sum", 0) or 0),
                                        str(r.get("node", ""))))


def fact_words(r):
    """A fact row's word stems: its claim and its predicate."""
    return stems(str(r.get("claim") or "") + " " + str(r.get("predicate") or ""))


def hop_spelled(via, by_subject):
    """Whether an edge of the walk spells the hop the question asks for.

    It does where an edge into a node with facts carries a question word none
    of that node's facts carries -- "business partners" for "the business
    partner of my family doctor": the hop is found, and a node reached over
    another edge is no answer. An edge that only repeats a word of its node's
    facts ("Lena lives with Jonas", "x heard Val works as a midwife") spells
    the answer, not the hop."""
    for k, words in (via or {}).items():
        rows = [r for r in by_subject.get(k) or () if r.get("claim")]
        if words and rows and set(words) - set().union(*(fact_words(r) for r in rows)):
            return True
    return False


def rank_node_facts(fact_rows, text, cap, names=(), via=None, strict=True):
    """A node's facts, the ones the question asks about first.

    Source first, then the question, then time (kern2 fix round 3, coordinator
    guard rail: a graph hit never ranks an older fact or hearsay before the
    current first-hand one): every first-hand fact before any `hearsay`; within
    that, the facts that share a word stem with the question -- names out
    (`name_stems`) -- before the facts that only share a VALUE the best of them
    names (its capitalised words past the first: "they live in Leipzig" leads to
    "they moved from Leipzig to Tromso", the statement that changed it and
    shares no word with the question); within that, the newest. Whether a fact
    shares one question word or three is no rank: measured (K2-M
    stale_vs_current-73/74), the count was the name, and it put "lives in Lyon"
    (2025-04-04) and two rumours before "still live in Krakow" (2025-06-20).
    """
    out = name_stems(names) | TIME_STEMS
    q = stems(text) - out
    own = fact_words
    # `via`: the question words the edges INTO this node carry (None = the
    # question names the node, or a walk from before this fix). A fact of a
    # node the question did not name takes a seat only when the edge adds a
    # question word the fact does not have -- "the flatmate (edge) ... live
    # (fact)". Measured (K2-M stale_vs_current-62): a rumour edge "Jonas heard
    # Leopold drives an orange Citroen" carried "drive" and seated Leopold's
    # cars for "What car does Henrik Falkner drive now?".
    # Deep review of kf89 (N4): that strictness holds where the question names
    # a rank-0 anchor (the Citroen case) or an edge of the walk spells the hop
    # (`hop_spelled`: "business partners" -- a node reached over a flatmate
    # edge or a rumour that names the job is no answer, probe multihop-34);
    # that is `strict`. Where neither holds, a first-hand fact that carries a
    # question word of its own keeps its seat too -- the extractor's wording
    # of the edge ("Y lives with X" instead of "flatmates") must not decide
    # whether the hop answers ("where does the flatmate of my grandson live
    # now?" lost the answer: via ['live']).
    if via is not None and any(r.get("claim") for r in fact_rows):
        fact_rows = [r for r in fact_rows if set(via) - own(r)
                     or (not strict and q & own(r) and not hearsay(r))]
    # A question about NOW seats no first-hand value a newer first-hand value of
    # the same axis replaced: "lives in Lyon" (2025-04-04) and "still live in
    # Krakow" (2025-06-20) are one axis (`canonical_predicate` lives_in), and
    # with both seated the old one out-voted the current one in the fusion
    # (K2-M stale_vs_current-73/74, multihop-25: Bremen before Salzburg). The
    # keyword leg still carries the old value -- a history question loses
    # nothing -- and a rumour never replaces anything.
    if TIME_STEMS & stems(text):
        latest = {}
        for r in fact_rows:
            ax = str(r.get("canonical_predicate") or r.get("predicate") or "")
            # Review T3: an empty `valid_from` is UNKNOWN, not the oldest time --
            # it neither replaces a value nor is replaced by one.
            if ax and not hearsay(r) and str(r.get("valid_from") or ""):
                latest[ax] = max(latest.get(ax, ""), str(r.get("valid_from") or ""))
        fact_rows = [r for r in fact_rows if hearsay(r) or not str(r.get("valid_from") or "")
                     or str(r.get("valid_from") or "") >= latest.get(
                         str(r.get("canonical_predicate") or r.get("predicate") or ""), "")]
    def newest(r):
        return (_neg(str(r.get("valid_from") or "")), str(r.get("id")))
    first = sorted(fact_rows, key=lambda r: (not q & own(r), hearsay(r), newest(r)))
    vals = set()
    if first and q & own(first[0]):
        words = str(first[0].get("claim") or "").split()[1:]
        vals = stems(" ".join(w for w in words if w[:1].isupper())) - q - out
    ranked = sorted(fact_rows, key=lambda r: (hearsay(r), not q & own(r), not vals & own(r),
                                              newest(r)))
    # A fact that shares nothing with the question nor with the value it asks
    # about gets no seat: measured (mini boundary test, multihop), the newest
    # small talk of a walked node displaced keyword hits in the fusion. Rows
    # without a claim (a page from before #1057) keep the old behaviour.
    if any(r.get("claim") for r in fact_rows):
        ranked = [r for r in ranked if (q | vals) & own(r)]
    # Where a first-hand fact answers, a rumour gets no graph seat at all: its
    # vote lifted it over the first-hand answer in the fusion (K2-M probe
    # stale_vs_current-64 offline: "Marta had heard ... works as a midwife"
    # before "still work as a beekeeper"). The keyword leg still carries it,
    # rendered as what its source says.
    if any(q & own(r) and not hearsay(r) for r in ranked):
        ranked = [r for r in ranked if not hearsay(r)]
    return ranked[:cap]


def _neg(s):
    return tuple(-ord(ch) for ch in s)


def tokens_of(text):
    """Query tokens for FTS and for the graph anchors. Deterministic, LLM-free.

    This CUTS WORDS, it does not fold them. Folding belongs to exactly one
    place -- the store's FTS5 tokenizer, which wraps `unicode61` and therefore
    case-folds and strips diacritics on the indexed text and on this query text
    alike. A fold here would be a SECOND one, on a query the index side then
    folds again, and the two would stop meeting.

    So the separator class is the Unicode-aware word class: a letter of ANY
    script, a digit, the underscore, plus the hyphen a compound name is written
    with. GH #518: the class used to read `[^0-9A-Za-zaeoeueAEOEUEss_-]`, whose
    tail is the ASCII SPELLING of the German umlauts -- ae, oe, ue, ss -- every
    letter of which `A-Za-z` already covers. The class therefore added nothing
    and the real characters landed in the SEPARATOR half: a German word came
    back as a fragment (Soehne -> `hne`) or, once both fragments fell under the
    three-character floor below, as nothing at all (Groesse -> nothing). The
    keyword leg then asked FTS5 for a term the index does not hold, and the
    graph anchors -- matched exactly against entity names -- named nobody.
    """
    raw = [t for t in re.split(r"[^\w-]+", text, flags=re.UNICODE) if len(t) >= 3]
    return [t for t in raw if t.lower() not in STOP]


def fts_match(text):
    """FTS5 query built from quoted tokens — caller text never reaches the
    matcher unquoted (it would be read as FTS operator syntax)."""
    toks = [t.replace('"', "") for t in tokens_of(text)]
    # R7: trailing prefix, so a singular query token still reaches the plural
    # index term. No prefix at the word START -- FTS5 cannot do that without a
    # trigram tokenizer, and that would be a schema break. The stop-word filter
    # and the quoting are untouched by this.
    # #88: the cap takes the tokens of the surviving TAIL. Taking them from
    # the head kept exactly the wrong half of a contaminated query -- and
    # after the hygiene guard the tail IS the question. A query at or below
    # the cap is untouched by this.
    return " OR ".join('"%s"*' % t for t in toks[-QUERY_TOKENS:])


def bm25_floor(rows):
    """#297: drop the keyword hits the leg's OWN best hit dwarfs.

    `search` returns a `rank` column (SQLite `bm25`, SMALLER IS BETTER, normally
    negative). The floor is a fraction of the best rank ON THIS PAGE, so the two
    keyword sub-searches are never measured against each other's scale: a
    shallow fact page and a deep episode page each get their own cut.

    Three ways out without cutting, all the same rule the semantic floor follows
    -- a floor without a scale is a guess, and a guess must not cut. A page whose
    best rank is not negative carries no usable signal at all (an absent, null or
    zero rank is not a bm25 score); a ratio of 0 is the ablation knob; and a row
    whose own rank is missing or not a number is left where it is rather than
    judged against a scale it never joined.
    """
    ranks = [float(r["rank"]) for r in rows
             if isinstance(r.get("rank"), (int, float))
             and not isinstance(r.get("rank"), bool)]
    if not ranks or KW_MIN_SCORE_RATIO == 0:
        return rows
    best = min(ranks)
    if best >= 0:
        return rows
    floor = best * KW_MIN_SCORE_RATIO
    return [r for r in rows
            if not isinstance(r.get("rank"), (int, float))
            or isinstance(r.get("rank"), bool)
            or float(r["rank"]) <= floor]


def fmt_day(ts):
    """Day granularity for the rendered text block (O-5).

    Since #296 the JSON bundle beside the text carries days too, so the exact
    instant lives in `recall_diagnostic` -- one hop away, in the same message,
    which the message log stores whole. The line a reader sees carries the day,
    which is the resolution a "what was it before?" question is answered at.
    """
    return str(ts or "")[:10]

# THAT file is the authority; a script cannot import, so the twin is pinned
# instead: crates/meclaw-cells/tests/p6_bundle_dedup.rs runs both over the same
# table and compares, so the two cannot drift apart unnoticed. Same three effects
# in the same order: case fold, Latin-1 composition (NFD -> NFC), whitespace
# collapse over the store's own whitespace (GH #948: Python's `str.split()` also
# splits on U+001C..U+001F, which the store keeps). The writer carries the same
# text for its alias check; gh948 holds the two copies byte-equal. One definition of "normalised" everywhere -- a collapse in the bundle
# must never mean something else than a merge in the store.
# Keep the two anchor comments.
COMPOSE_ROWS = (
    ("\u0300", "aeiou", "\u00e0\u00e8\u00ec\u00f2\u00f9"),
    ("\u0301", "aeiouy", "\u00e1\u00e9\u00ed\u00f3\u00fa\u00fd"),
    ("\u0302", "aeiou", "\u00e2\u00ea\u00ee\u00f4\u00fb"),
    ("\u0303", "ano", "\u00e3\u00f1\u00f5"),
    ("\u0308", "aeiouy", "\u00e4\u00eb\u00ef\u00f6\u00fc\u00ff"),
    ("\u030a", "a", "\u00e5"),
    ("\u0327", "c", "\u00e7"),
)
COMPOSITIONS = {(base, mark): composed
                for mark, bases, composed_forms in COMPOSE_ROWS
                for base, composed in zip(bases, composed_forms)}
# Rust's `char::is_whitespace` (the Unicode White_Space property), spelled out:
# Python's `str.split()` also splits on U+001C..U+001F, which the store keeps.
WHITE_SPACE = frozenset("\t\n\x0b\x0c\r \x85\xa0\u1680\u2000\u2001\u2002\u2003"
                        "\u2004\u2005\u2006\u2007\u2008\u2009\u200a\u2028\u2029"
                        "\u202f\u205f\u3000")


def normalize_text(value):
    """The normal form of one string -- the twin of `meclaw_norm` (0.2.0 P4).

    Same three effects in the same order as the store: case fold, Latin-1
    composition (NFD -> NFC), whitespace collapse over the store's own
    whitespace. An unrecognised mark leaves the two spellings DIFFERENT, which
    is the same conservatism the Rust side ships.
    """
    out = []
    for ch in str(value or "").lower():
        composed = COMPOSITIONS.get((out[-1], ch)) if out else None
        if composed is None:
            out.append(ch)
        else:
            out[-1] = composed
    words, word = [], []
    for ch in out:
        if ch in WHITE_SPACE:
            if word:
                words.append("".join(word))
                word = []
        else:
            word.append(ch)
    if word:
        words.append("".join(word))
    return " ".join(words)

def episode_ord(row):
    """Recency of one episode copy -- the order the collapse survivor is picked by
    (#15). Event time first, ingest instant second, id last so the order is total.
    """
    return (str(row.get("happened_at") or ""), str(row.get("recorded_at") or ""),
            str(row.get("id") or ""))


def fold_episodes(hits, rows_by_id):
    """GH #691: one rank position per NORMAL FORM in a query leg.

    Measured live: ten copies of one question took ten of the twenty positions of
    the semantic leg, and the fact that answered it never entered the leg. The
    #15 collapse in `t1-emit` folds such copies too, but only AFTER the fusion --
    by then they had already spent the leg. So a query leg folds its own page:
    the survivor keeps the BEST rank (the first copy on the page) and becomes the
    NEWEST copy (`episode_ord`, the same recency #15 picks by); its siblings
    travel as `copies`, so `t1-emit` can still say how often it was asked. A
    fold that dropped them would turn `(seen: 5)` into `(seen: 1)` -- the T12
    scenario pins exactly that count. An empty normal form is no identity, so it
    never folds, and a hit with no row in hand is left where it is.
    """
    out, slot = [], {}
    for h in hits:
        row = rows_by_id.get(str(h.get("id"))) if h.get("kind") == "episode" else None
        key = normalize_text(row.get("content")) if row else ""
        if not key:
            out.append(h)
            continue
        if key not in slot:
            slot[key] = len(out)
            out.append(dict(h, copies=[h["id"]], _ord=episode_ord(row)))
            continue
        s = out[slot[key]]
        s["copies"].append(h["id"])
        if episode_ord(row) > s["_ord"]:
            s["id"], s["_ord"] = h["id"], episode_ord(row)
    for h in out:
        h.pop("_ord", None)
        if len(h.get("copies") or []) < 2:
            h.pop("copies", None)
    return out


def adopt_episode(cand, ep_id, row):
    """The NEWEST copy takes over the identity of a collapsed line (#15).

    The SLOT belongs to the best-ranked copy: rank, score and the merged legs stay
    untouched, so a collapse never re-ranks. What moves is what a reader would
    otherwise read wrong -- id, wording, sender, session and instant now describe
    the copy the bundle actually shows, because a repetition is interesting for
    when it LAST happened.
    """
    cand["id"] = ep_id
    cand["text"] = str(row.get("content") or "")
    cand["sender"] = said_by(row)
    cand["session_id"] = row.get("session_id")
    cand["happened_at"] = row.get("happened_at")
    # GH #936: the mark belongs to the copy shown, like everything above.
    cand["affect"] = parse_mark(row.get("affect"))


def superseded_marker(row, axis_rows, as_of):
    """The currency marker of a candidate line -- the inverse of `previously:`
    (statement identity W1, ruling Q6).

    `previously:` says what a candidate REPLACED. The missing half is the other
    direction: a candidate whose own statement the store has closed has to say
    so, or the bundle hands a superseded value to the model with nothing marking
    it -- measured, that is the one wrong answer of the 0.2.0 P8a slice. Dropping
    such a candidate instead is not the alternative: it would destroy history
    questions and hide the store's own uncertainty.

    The verdict comes from the STORED columns, and that is what makes this the
    inverse of `previously:`: `expired_at`/`superseded_by` are what a dream run
    MATERIALISED, not what this request derived. A closure in the future of the
    read instant has not happened yet (spec D.5), so an as-of bundle never leaks
    a later value through its own annotation.

    Returns None when nothing closed the statement, the claim of the newer
    statement when the axis page carries it, and the empty string when it does
    not -- a closure without a reachable successor is still a closure, and THAT
    is the half that changes the answer.
    """
    end = str(row.get("expired_at") or "")
    if not end or end > as_of:
        return None
    successor = str(row.get("superseded_by") or "")
    if successor:
        for r in axis_rows or []:
            if str(r.get("id")) == successor:
                return str(r.get("claim") or "")
    return ""


def sessions_view(cands):
    """The candidates grouped by session, sessions in the order they happened.

    #148: a multi-session answer is an aggregation over sessions, and the flat
    ranked list is the one shape that hides which candidates belong together.
    The measurement is unambiguous -- 100 % of the gold sessions retrieved,
    30.8 % of the answers right -- and the difference between those two numbers
    is structure, not evidence.

    Nothing here retrieves anything. It is the same candidates, seen along the
    axis the question is asking about. A candidate with no session (a fact
    written before the column, a belief) lands in `unattributed` rather than
    being dropped: an unknown origin is not evidence of a shared one.

    Sorted by first instant, with the id-sorted fallback for rows whose instant
    is missing -- a stable order matters more than a perfect one, because the
    model reads this list as a timeline.
    """
    groups = collections.OrderedDict()
    for c in cands:
        key = str(c.get("session_id") or "") or "unattributed"
        g = groups.setdefault(key, {"session_id": key, "candidates": [],
                                    "first": None, "last": None})
        g["candidates"].append(c["id"])
        when = c.get("happened_at") or c.get("valid_from") or ""
        if when:
            if g["first"] is None or when < g["first"]:
                g["first"] = when
            if g["last"] is None or when > g["last"]:
                g["last"] = when
    out = [dict(g, n=len(g["candidates"])) for g in groups.values()]
    out.sort(key=lambda g: (g["first"] is None, g["first"] or "", g["session_id"]))
    return out


def history_entries(c, cap=1):
    """The predecessors a candidate SHOWS -- the same answer for every renderer (#296).

    R4/P15, and since ruling S6 for BOTH halves of the message: ONE predecessor,
    the claim this one replaced and the day it ended. The chain is sorted by
    start, so the last entry is the immediately preceding claim; everything older
    is the history OF that history and answers a question nobody asked this round.

    Until S6 the cut lived on the JSON side alone and the rendered text beside it
    ended a superseded line with the whole chain -- two deliberate decisions that
    disagreed, in one script, both citing the same wave. Both halves travel in the
    SAME prompt, so on a long-lived axis the saving #296 measured was partly given
    back one slot over. This is now the one place either renderer may ask, which
    is what keeps them from parting again.

    What leaves here is not lost: `recall_diagnostic.candidates[].history` carries
    the record the loop built, in the SAME message, and this function never
    touches it -- it reads a candidate and returns a new list.

    Defensive about the shape for the same reason every other reader in this
    script is: a hit whose chain select was truncated arrives without predecessors
    rather than with a guessed one, and a candidate that is not a fact carries no
    `history` key at all.
    """
    history = c.get("history") or []
    if not isinstance(history, list) or not history:
        return []
    return history[-cap:]


def said_of(fact):
    """The claim of a fact AS a reader may take it (GH #849, owner ruling R-SN-4).

    A fact whose `source` names a participant is what that participant SAID, and
    it is rendered as exactly that: "<ref> says: <claim>". The reference is the
    participant reference affinity mints (the `roster` legend of the round turns
    it into a name), so the words never read as the member's own statement and
    never as settled knowledge. A fact without a source reads as it always did:
    the claim value itself, untouched.
    """
    claim = fact.get("claim")
    source = str(fact.get("source") or "")
    if not source:
        return claim
    return "%s says: %s" % (named_ref(fact, source), "" if claim is None else claim)


def named_ref(fact, source):
    """GH #1039: `Name (peer <ref>)` once the reference is bound to a name.

    A peer's self-statement is filed under the subject `peer <ref>`
    (extract-glue `peer_subject`), and the alias table binds that spelling to
    the participant's name, so its `canonical_subject` IS the name (in the
    store's lower-cased normal form, title-cased back here). An unbound
    reference, and a fact about somebody else, keep the bare reference."""
    key = " ".join(str(fact.get("subject") or "").lower().split())
    name = str(fact.get("canonical_subject") or "")
    if key != "peer " + source.lower() or not name or name == key:
        return source
    return "%s (peer %s)" % (title_name(name), source)


def title_name(name):
    return " ".join(w[:1].upper() + w[1:] for w in name.split())


# GH #849 fix round 1 (review I1): the participant reference affinity mints --
# 8 hex characters, 12 on a collision (M1 section 2.1). A belief's `observer`
# in this form is the peer whose statements the belief rests on; any other
# value (empty, a model's free text) renders as before.
PARTICIPANT_REF = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-f]{8}([0-9a-f]{4})?$")


def belief_said(row):
    """A belief AS a reader may take it (GH #849 fix round 1, review I1).

    The night derives a belief's source from the facts it rests on and names a
    single peer source in `observer` (dream-glue `belief_source`). Such a belief
    is that participant's view, rendered the way `said_of` renders their facts:
    "<ref> says: <statement>". Everything else reads as it always did.
    """
    statement = row.get("statement")
    observer = str(row.get("observer") or "")
    if not PARTICIPANT_REF.match(observer):
        return statement
    return "%s says: %s" % (observer, "" if statement is None else statement)


def said_by(row):
    """WHO a turn is, as a reader sees it (GH #849 fix round 1, review M5).

    A peer's turn names the peer: `peer <ref>`, the form the close pass renders
    its turns in. Every other turn -- and a peer turn that arrived without its
    reference -- keeps its bare role.
    """
    sender = row.get("sender")
    speaker = str(row.get("speaker") or "")
    if str(sender or "") == "peer" and speaker:
        # GH #1039: the name the channel knew the peer by, when the turn had one.
        name = " ".join(str(row.get("speaker_name") or "").split())
        return ("%s (peer %s)" % (name, speaker)) if name else "peer " + speaker
    return sender


def render_candidate_line(c):
    """The ONE place a tier-1/2 candidate becomes a line of the bundle text (O-5).

    Since P15 every fact candidate carries either its predecessors (`history`,
    point mode) or the span it was valid for (`span`, window mode) -- but the
    model reads THIS text, not the JSON beside it, so a line that renders the
    claim alone drops the temporal answer on the floor. A candidate with neither
    field renders byte for byte as it did before this function existed.
    """
    # R3: the AXIS in front of the value. The JSON beside this text has carried
    # `subject` and `predicate` on every fact candidate since P15, but the model
    # reads THIS line -- and a bare object never says WHICH question it answers:
    # a favourite city, a birthplace and a next destination all render as the
    # same word. Half an axis renders the half that is there (same conservatism
    # as `axis_key`/`subject_key`), and a candidate with neither -- every
    # episode, and a fact row from before the columns -- renders byte for byte
    # as it did before.
    axis = " ".join(str(p) for p in (c.get("subject"), c.get("predicate")) if p)
    line = "- [%s %s] %s" % (c["kind"], "/".join(c["legs"]),
                             "%s: %s" % (axis, c["text"]) if axis else c["text"])
    return line + candidate_annotations(c)


def candidate_annotations(c):
    """The annotations that can turn a right answer into a wrong one (#281).

    Both renderers of this script end a row with these, in this order, out of
    THIS function: the diagnostic line (`render_candidate_line`) and the
    readable sections a model reads (`render_payload_lines`). One place, because
    two renderers that describe the same candidate differently are worse than
    either of them alone -- whoever reads the trace to explain an answer has to
    see what the answer was read off.

    Each annotation is absent unless the candidate carries it, so a row that has
    nothing to qualify renders byte for byte as it did before any of them
    existed. Reading order: what kind of statement it is, how long it held,
    whether it still holds, whether that can be vouched for at all, what it
    replaced, and how often it was said.
    """
    out = ""
    # GH #67: an INTENTION renders as one. The speech act left the predicate --
    # a plan about a matter now sits on the matter's own axis, marked on the
    # STATEMENT by `fact_kind` -- so a line that renders a plan like a fact would
    # hand the model a goal as an accomplished thing. Directly behind the value,
    # because it qualifies the value and not the span or the history; absent for
    # world and experience, so every other line renders byte for byte as before.
    intent = c.get("intent")
    if intent:
        out += " (%s)" % intent
    span = c.get("span")
    if isinstance(span, dict):
        lo = fmt_day(span.get("from"))
        hi = fmt_day(span.get("until")) or "open"
        if lo or hi != "open":
            out += " [%s -> %s]" % (lo, hi)
    # W1 (ruling Q6): the currency marker, in the same shape as the annotations
    # around it and absent unless the store closed this statement -- a line
    # without it renders byte for byte as it did before.
    superseded = c.get("superseded")
    if superseded:
        out += " (superseded by: %s)" % superseded
    elif superseded is not None:
        out += " (superseded: yes)"
    # R7 (Nachtrag 3): the model reads THIS line, so the flag has to be in it --
    # a candidate rendered without it reads as current, which is the wrong answer
    # the flag exists to prevent. The wording says what is unknown and nothing
    # about what was removed.
    if c.get("supersession_unknown"):
        out += " (currency unknown: cannot vouch that this still holds)"
    # #296 (ruling S6): the ONE predecessor `history_entries` allows -- the same
    # claim the JSON payload beside this text names, out of the same function. The
    # join survives the cut, so the SHAPE of the annotation is unchanged and every
    # line with at most one predecessor renders byte for byte as it did before.
    history = history_entries(c)
    if history:
        out += " (previously: %s)" % "; ".join(
            "%s until %s" % (h.get("claim"), fmt_day(h.get("until")))
            if h.get("until") else str(h.get("claim"))
            for h in history)
    # #15: a collapsed line SAYS how many copies it stands for. Same shape as the
    # history annotation, and absent at count 1, so every line that never repeated
    # renders byte for byte as it did before the collapse existed.
    seen = int(c.get("seen") or 1)
    if seen > 1:
        out += " (seen: %d)" % seen
    return out


# The head of the said section, and the whole of what #537 adds. The header says
# how the lines were PRODUCED -- verbatim, not interpreted -- and nothing about
# what they are worth. A past turn is a record of that turn: an assistant
# sentence claiming something is not stored is evidence about that answer and
# about nothing else, and the FACTS section right above it may say the opposite.
#
# Measured on a live hive during #536: three such lines stood in a bundle, the
# model repeated them, and its answer was written back as a fourth -- a loop in
# which every failed round makes the next one more certain the memory is empty.
# #536 removed the trigger; the material is still here.
#
# ITS OWN LINE, not a longer header. The header is a pinned public string (#281)
# quoted in three tests and in the template README, and a reader that matches it
# keeps matching it. It is written so it holds with or without a FACTS section
# above -- naming a section that may be absent would be a dangling reference in
# exactly the bundle that needs the line most.
SAID_CAVEAT = ("  (an earlier answer claiming something is NOT stored is"
               " evidence about that answer and nothing else -- never a"
               " measurement of this memory)")


def render_payload_lines(cands):
    """The ONE place the candidates become the text a MODEL reads (#281).

    The kind is the SECTION, not a bracket in front of the row. That bracket
    (`- [fact keyword] ...`) mixed two questions that have nothing to do with
    each other: WHAT a row is -- a derived, canonical, dated statement, or a
    sentence somebody actually said -- and WHICH retrieval leg nominated it. The
    second one answers nothing a reader asked and travels in
    `recall_diagnostic`; the first one decides how the row may be USED, and a
    label a reader has to decode is a label a reader gets wrong.

    The failure this fixes is a past QUESTION rendered like an asserted fact:
    "what is my favourite colour?" in the same shape as a claim. So an utterance
    opens with the speaker and the day it was said, in quotes, under a header
    that says it is verbatim and not interpreted -- three signals that it is
    evidence about a conversation, never an answer to the question.

    A section with no rows is omitted: a header is a promise that something
    follows it, and an empty one costs budget and invites the model to wonder
    what it missed.

    Reads the INTERNAL records, not the payload dicts -- the two describe the
    same candidates and the record is the one that still has every field. Half
    an axis renders the half that is there, the same conservatism
    `render_candidate_line` and `payload_candidate` follow, and a fact whose
    columns predate the axis renders as the bare claim rather than as a dangling
    `=`.
    """
    lines = []
    facts = [c for c in cands if c.get("kind") == "fact"]
    said = [c for c in cands if c.get("kind") != "fact"]
    if facts:
        lines.append("FACTS (extracted, canonical, dated)")
        for c in facts:
            axis = " ".join(str(p) for p in (c.get("subject"), c.get("predicate")) if p)
            line = "  %s = %s" % (axis, c["text"]) if axis else "  %s" % c["text"]
            since = fmt_day(c.get("valid_from"))
            if since:
                line += "   since %s" % since
            lines.append(line + candidate_annotations(c))
    if said:
        lines.append("WHAT WAS SAID (verbatim, not interpreted)")
        lines.append(SAID_CAVEAT)
        for c in said:
            # Who and when, in front of the words. Either half may be missing --
            # a turn without a sender is still evidence -- and what is missing
            # is left out rather than filled in with a guess.
            head = " on ".join(p for p in (str(c.get("sender") or ""),
                                           fmt_day(c.get("happened_at"))) if p)
            line = '  %s: "%s"' % (head, c["text"]) if head else '  "%s"' % c["text"]
            lines.append(line + candidate_annotations(c))
    return lines


def empty_state_sentence(as_of, fused):
    """The one sentence a bundle with no candidate says about itself (#297).

    A recall that found nothing used to emit the asserting header and no
    rows. A model handed that reads it as "the lookup ran, this is what
    memory holds" and answers the question from somewhere else -- which is
    the invention the bundle exists to prevent. So the empty case states the
    RESULT instead of framing an absent list, and it names the one
    distinction a reader cannot make from an empty list alone:

      * nothing about this was stored -- the gap is in what memory HOLDS;
      * something was stored and none of it was close enough -- the legs
        answered and every hit died at a relevance floor (#297: the keyword
        ratio and the semantic coin flip). That is a gap in how the QUESTION
        fits this store, not in the store.

    `leg_sizes` reports 0 for both, so the pre-floor `leg_sizes_raw` map
    decides -- read DEFENSIVELY: a request in flight when the floors landed
    carries no raw map at all, and a leg whose raw count predates its own
    floor can report LESS than the floored one. Missing raw information is
    never a floor claim, and the count is a max per leg, never a subtraction
    that could go negative.

    `semantic_degraded` is deliberately NOT read here. The floor empties the
    semantic list and raises that flag exactly as a dead embedder does; a
    sentence built on it would report broken machinery for a healthy run
    whose hits were merely far away. The raw count is the discriminator, and
    the flag itself stays in `recall_diagnostic` for whoever debugs the
    embedder -- which is a question about the RUN, not about the answer.
    """
    sizes = fused.get("leg_sizes") or {}
    raws = fused.get("leg_sizes_raw") or {}

    def size(m, name):
        try:
            return max(int(m.get(name) or 0), 0)
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            return 0

    gated = sum(size(sizes, n) for n in LEG_ORDER)
    raw = sum(max(size(raws, n), size(sizes, n)) for n in LEG_ORDER)
    day = fmt_day(as_of)
    if gated == 0 and raw > 0:
        return ("Nothing in this memory answers this question (as of %s): "
                "%d stored %s came back for it and none of them cleared the "
                "relevance floor -- every one of them was too far from the "
                "question to stand as an answer."
                % (day, raw, "hit" if raw == 1 else "hits"))
    return "Nothing in this memory answers this question (as of %s)." % day


def render_diagnostic_text(candidates, fused, tier):
    """The rendering the payload gave up, kept whole for whoever debugs (#279).

    Until this package this string WAS the bundle: a header naming the run and
    one flat, ranked line per candidate, each tagged with the legs that
    nominated it. Handed to a model it read as a search result and got
    discounted as one -- but handed to a person explaining afterwards why THAT
    candidate came back, it is exactly the right document. Two readers, two
    documents; the issue asks for the second one to MOVE, never for it to go,
    and "the bookkeeping is exactly what makes a bundle debuggable" is its own
    sentence.

    Byte for byte what the emit block produced before, out of the unchanged
    `render_candidate_line`. `tier` is the tier the bundle is SERVED at -- a
    `t2-downgrade` answers at tier 1 -- which is what this line has always said.
    """
    lines = ["MEMORY (tier %s, %d candidates, RRF over %s)"
             % (tier, len(candidates),
                ",".join(fused.get("legs_present", [])) or "no leg")]
    for c in candidates:
        lines.append(render_candidate_line(c))
    return "\n".join(lines)


def payload_candidate(c):
    """The ONE place an internal candidate record becomes the JSON a model reads
    (#296).

    Two audiences, two shapes. The record the loop builds is the RETRIEVAL's own
    bookkeeping -- the row id, the fused score, the legs that nominated it, the
    rank it holds, the session it was said in, the whole version chain. A reader
    answering a question can do nothing with any of it, and every byte of it is
    prompt budget the answer does not get. What leaves here is not lost:
    `recall_diagnostic` carries the record verbatim in the SAME message, and
    that is the only reason this may take anything out at all.

    Built as a NEW dict, never by deleting from the record: payload and
    diagnostic share one list, so a mutation here would shrink the trace along
    with the payload -- and the saving would cost exactly the debuggability it
    was paid for.

    Instants arrive as DAYS, through the same `fmt_day` the rendered line uses:
    the resolution a "since when?" question is answered at, and the same answer
    in both halves of the message.

    Keys are ABSENT when unknown, the discipline the record's own optional keys
    already follow -- a candidate that knows nothing pays no byte for saying so.
    """
    out = {"kind": c.get("kind"), "text": c.get("text")}
    # GH #936: absent unless known -- the discipline of every key below.
    if c.get("affect") is not None:
        out["affect"] = c["affect"]
    if c.get("kind") != "fact":
        # An episode is a turn: who said it, and on which day. Its id, its
        # session and the exact instant are the trace's business.
        if c.get("sender"):
            out["who"] = c["sender"]
        when = fmt_day(c.get("happened_at"))
        if when:
            out["when"] = when
        # #15: absent at count 1, exactly like the rendered line.
        if int(c.get("seen") or 1) > 1:
            out["seen"] = int(c["seen"])
        return out
    # R3: the axis in front of the value -- the two keys that say WHICH question
    # this candidate answers. Half an axis travels as the half that is there,
    # the same conservatism `render_candidate_line` follows.
    for key in ("subject", "predicate"):
        if c.get(key):
            out[key] = c[key]
    since = fmt_day(c.get("valid_from"))
    if since:
        out["since"] = since
    # #280: validity still travels in both directions -- but as the CLOSURE and
    # as a day. The successor's id is a row name and says nothing to a reader,
    # so it stays in the trace next to the id of the candidate itself.
    until = fmt_day(c.get("valid_until"))
    if until:
        out["until"] = until
    for key in ("confidence", "intent", "supersession_unknown", "source"):
        if key in c:
            out[key] = c[key]
    # W1 (ruling Q6): present-and-empty is an answer of its own -- closed, with
    # no successor anyone can name -- so this key is copied by PRESENCE, not by
    # truth.
    if "superseded" in c:
        out["superseded"] = c["superseded"]
    if isinstance(c.get("span"), dict):
        out["span"] = {"from": fmt_day(c["span"].get("from")) or None,
                       "until": fmt_day(c["span"].get("until")) or None}
    # R4/P15, and since ruling S6 out of the SAME function the rendered line asks:
    # one predecessor, the claim this one replaced. The argument for the cut lives
    # on `history_entries` now, because it is the argument of both renderers and a
    # reason written down twice is a reason two paths can drift apart on.
    history = history_entries(c)
    if history:
        prev = history[-1]
        entry = {"claim": prev.get("claim")}
        end = fmt_day(prev.get("until"))
        if end:
            entry["until"] = end
        out["previously"] = [entry]
    return out

CORE_SINGLE = ["born_on", "diet", "favorite_color", "favorite_food", "favorite_music",
               "job_title", "lives_in", "partner_of", "preferred_language", "pronouns",
               "relationship_status", "timezone", "works_at"]
CORE_MULTI = ["allergic_to", "dislikes", "friend_of", "has_child", "has_parent",
              "has_pet", "has_sibling", "likes", "lived_in", "member_of", "owns",
              "skilled_in", "speaks_language", "studied_at", "visited", "worked_at"]
