                       "row": {"request_id": rid, "leg": "beliefs",
                               "payload": json.dumps(legs["beliefs"]),
                               "created_at": now, "fired": 0}}))
    if fact_ids:
        # No expired_at filter any more (R1/R4): supersession is DERIVED from the
        # version chain at read time, so a superseded hit is not dropped here --
        # t1-emit projects it onto its successor. A candidate without a hydration
        # row is still dropped there.
        calls.append(("r-hyd-fact",
                      {"operation": "select", "table": "facts",
                       "columns": ["id", "episode_id", "subject", "canonical_subject",
                                   "predicate", "canonical_predicate", "claim",
                                   "fact_kind", "valid_from", "valid_until",
                                   "expired_at", "superseded_by", "confidence",
                                   "channel", "audience_set", "source", "closure_source", "muted_at", "unmuted_at", "mute_words"],
                       "where": {"id": {"in": fact_ids}}}))
    if ep_ids:
        calls.append(("r-hyd-ep",
                      {"operation": "select", "table": "episodes",
                       "columns": ["id", "session_id", "sender", "speaker", "content",
                                   "happened_at", "recorded_at",
                                   "channel", "audience_set", "affect", "closure_source", "muted_at", "unmuted_at", "mute_words", "speaker_name"],
                       "where": {"id": {"in": ep_ids}}}))
    if subjects and predicates:
        # R3: ONE additional select carries every axis of every fact hit. The
        # store has no GROUP BY and answers one result set per op, so a select
        # per candidate would be up to LEG_LIMIT extra round trips. The `in`
        # cross product can return axes nobody asked for --
        # `project_fact_candidate` matches on the PAIR, so those are dropped in
        # code.
        calls.append(("r-hyd-axis",
                      {"operation": "select", "table": "facts",
                       "columns": ["id", "subject", "canonical_subject", "predicate",
                                   "canonical_predicate", "claim", "canonical_claim",
                                   "valid_from", "valid_until", "recorded_at",
                                   "expired_at", "superseded_by", "episode_id",
                                   "session_id", "fact_kind", "confidence",
                                   "channel", "audience_set", "source", "closure_source", "muted_at", "unmuted_at", "mute_words"],
                       "where": {"canonical_subject": {"in": subjects},
                                 "canonical_predicate": {"in": predicates}},
                       "order_by": [{"col": "valid_from", "dir": "asc"},
                                    {"col": "recorded_at", "dir": "asc"},
                                    {"col": "id", "dir": "asc"}],
                       "limit": AXIS_LIMIT}))
        # W5 (#13, ruling Q3): the judged cardinality of exactly these relations,
        # fired WITH the axis page rather than after it. Both are answers this
        # request needs before it can project a hit, and neither reads the other.
        calls.append(("r-hyd-card",
                      {"operation": "select", "table": "predicate_cardinality",
                       "columns": ["canonical_predicate", "verdict"],
                       "where": {"canonical_predicate": {"in": predicates}}}))
    # GH #936: the mark of every fact hit's SOURCE episode, one more call in
    # this bundle rather than one more store message (R1 counts messages). The
    # ids come from the rows the legs carried; a hit projected onto a successor
    # whose episode no leg carried reads as unknown -- a seventh message to know
    # it would break the budget for a case the successor's own hit covers.
    src_map = dict(store_legs.get("src") or {})
    for r in list((sem_aud or {}).values()) + list(graph_facts or []):
        if isinstance(r, dict) and r.get("id") and r.get("episode_id"):
            src_map[str(r.get("id"))] = str(r.get("episode_id"))
    src_ids = sorted({src_map[i] for i in fact_ids if src_map.get(i)})
    if src_ids:
        # The source episode is GATED like every row this request renders
        # (review I-1): a fact may be wider than the turn it came from (a `*`
        # fact, an imported or closer fact), and the mark is a statement about
        # that TURN. Its participant set rides in the same call, so the gate
        # costs no message.
        calls.append(("r-hyd-affect",
                      {"operation": "select", "table": "episodes",
                       "columns": ["id", "affect", "channel", "audience_set", "closure_source", "muted_at", "unmuted_at", "mute_words", "speaker_name"],
                       "where": {"id": {"in": src_ids}}}))
    # A missing leg is recognised at the READING end, not written as an empty
    # row: the trailing select sees the park in front of it, so a page that was
    # never asked for simply has no bundle leg -- and `bundle_rows` reads that as
    # the empty list the substitute insert used to stand for.
    calls.append(("r-hyd-read",
                  {"operation": "select", "table": "recall_scratch",
                   "columns": ["request_id", "leg", "payload", "fired"],
                   "where": {"request_id": rid, "leg": {"in": ["fused", "beliefs"]}}}))
    emit([store_bundle(calls, "t1-emit")])


# ============================================================ TIER 1 legs
if phase == "t1-fan" and op == "bundle":
    # The whole fan, answered in ONE reply. Every leg body below is the phase
    # body it used to be, word for word -- the gate, the bm25 floor, the anchor
    # names, the window cut, the `active` filter -- with exactly one change: the
    # rows come out of `bundle_rows(legs_doc, "r-fan-...")` instead of
    # `rows_of(d)`. A leg whose op was not in the bundle (no query tokens, no
    # tier 2) reads as the empty list the substitute inserts used to be.
    legs_doc = payloads_by_id(d)
    parked_legs = {}
    # --- keyword, episodes ---------------------------------------------------
    # Gated where the rows arrive, so the leg's rank list never contains a hit
    # nobody in this round may see -- ranks are RRF votes.
    page = bundle_rows(legs_doc, "r-fan-kw-ep")
    rows = visible_rows(page)
    # #297: the floor runs AFTER the gate and never instead of it -- a floor may
    # narrow what a round sees, never widen it. The count is taken between the
    # two: a PRE-gate count would leak the existence of rows this round is not
    # entitled to see into the empty-state sentence built from it.
    kw_ep_raw = len([r for r in rows if r.get("id")])
    rows = bm25_floor(rows)
    # #280 (item 3): the cap is measured on the PAGE, before the gate thinned it.
    # GH #691: copies of one question take ONE rank position here as in the
    # semantic leg (`fold_episodes`); the cap stays measured on the page.
    parked_legs["kw-ep"] = leg_payload(
        fold_episodes([{"kind": "episode", "id": r.get("id")} for r in rows if r.get("id")],
                      {str(r.get("id")): r for r in rows if r.get("id")}),
        len(page), LEG_LIMIT)
    parked_legs["kw-ep-raw"] = {"n": kw_ep_raw}
    # --- keyword, facts (+ the graph anchors it seeds) ------------------------
    # Gated BEFORE the anchors are read off the rows: an invisible fact must not
    # seed the graph leg either, or the gate would leak through the entity names
    # it hands on. Same for the floor.
    page = bundle_rows(legs_doc, "r-fan-kw-fact")
    rows = visible_rows(page)
    kw_fact_raw = len([r for r in rows if r.get("id")])
    rows = bm25_floor(rows)
    parked_legs["kw-fact"] = leg_payload(
        [{"kind": "fact", "id": r.get("id")} for r in rows if r.get("id")],
        len(page), LEG_LIMIT)
    parked_legs["kw-fact-raw"] = {"n": kw_fact_raw}
    # Graph anchors, LLM-free: query tokens (case variants, because `in` is
    # exact) plus the local parts of the subjects the keyword leg just found.
    names = set()
    for t in tokens_of(query):
        names.update([t, t.lower(), t.capitalize()])
    for r in rows[:LEG_LIMIT]:
        local = str(r.get("subject") or "").split(":")[-1]
        if local:
            names.update([local, local.lower(), local.capitalize()])
    # GH #536 deliberately does NOT put the asker here, and the reason is a
    # measurement rather than a principle. It was tried: the asker anchored the
    # walk, which did reach a subject spelling the audience token does not carry
    # (`member:alex` -> the edge `alex -> Alex Example` -> the facts written
    # under the fuller name). But an asker is a HUB, and a hub anchor is true of
    # every question: the walk came back full on every single one, and the leg
    # then voted at full weight for twenty rows the question never asked about.
    # Measured on a live hive, question "what colour are my eyes": the graph leg
    # returned 20 hits and put a weather fact about a city into the bundle. A
    # leg whose rank list is the same for every question is a constant, not a
    # retrieval. The asker belongs in a leg with a BUDGET (`self`), not in the
    # one leg whose whole value is that the question named its starting point.
    # GH #1057: name anchors and their rank -- 0 for what the question spells,
    # i+1 for a name off the i-th keyword hit (`rank_walk` weighs by it).
    anchor_rank = {}
    for n in name_anchors(query, []) | set(tokens_of(query)):
        anchor_rank.setdefault(n.lower(), 0)
    for i, r in enumerate(rows[:LEG_LIMIT]):
        own = name_anchors("", [r.get("claim")])
        local = str(r.get("subject") or "").split(":")[-1]
        if local:
            own.add(local)
        names.update(own)
        for n in own:
            anchor_rank.setdefault(n.lower(), i + 1)
    names.update(name_anchors(query, []))
    parked_legs["anchor_rank"] = anchor_rank
    ranked_anchors = sorted((n for n in names if n),
                            key=lambda n: (anchor_rank.get(n.lower(), 99), n))
    if len(ranked_anchors) > GRAPH_ANCHORS:
        sys.stderr.write("recall: %d name anchors, the entity join looks up the first %d "
                         "(tier1_graph_anchors)\n" % (len(ranked_anchors), GRAPH_ANCHORS))
        # GH #1098: the cut is the bundle's too (`graph_cuts`), not only stderr's.
        parked_legs["anchor_cut"] = [GRAPH_ANCHORS, len(ranked_anchors)]
    parked_legs["anchors"] = ranked_anchors[:GRAPH_ANCHORS]
    # --- the axis map (#418) -------------------------------------------------
    # The canonical keys of every fact this round can nominate, taken WHERE THE
    # ROWS ARE, so the axis page can be asked in the same bundle as the
    # hydration instead of one hop behind it. Post-gate, like everything else.
    axis = {str(r.get("id")): [subject_key(r), axis_key(r)] for r in rows if r.get("id")}
    # GH #936: the source episode of every fact this round can nominate, taken
    # where the rows are for the same reason as the axis: the mark lookup then
    # rides in the hydration bundle instead of one store message behind it.
    src = {str(r.get("id")): str(r.get("episode_id")) for r in rows
           if r.get("id") and r.get("episode_id")}
    # --- temporal ------------------------------------------------------------
    # Gated BEFORE the temporal cut, not instead of it: the audience rule is an
    # ADDITIONAL predicate, and `window_hits` still decides the span exactly as
    # before -- it just never sees a version this round was not present for.
    page = bundle_rows(legs_doc, "r-fan-temporal")
    rows = visible_rows(page)
    # The window is read again here rather than carried on a leg: the context
    # slot is persistent, so every phase of one request sees the same answer, and
    # a half-open window was already rejected at the request entry (R5).
    window = read_window(ctx)
    # #280 (item 3): this leg asks with two different limits -- LEG_LIMIT in
    # point mode, the generous AXIS_LIMIT of the window pre-filter -- so the cap
    # it reports has to be the one it actually asked with.
    temporal_limit = LEG_LIMIT if window is None else AXIS_LIMIT
    if window is None:
        rows = [r for r in rows
                if is_open(r.get("valid_until")) or str(r.get("valid_until")) > as_of]
    else:
        rows = window_hits(rows, window[0], window[1])
        # (valid_from desc, recorded_at desc, id asc): newest validity first, the
        # tie-break complete. Two stable passes, because a single reverse=True
        # would flip the id tie-break with the rest of the key.
        rows = sorted(rows, key=lambda r: str(r.get("id") or ""))
        rows = sorted(rows, key=lambda r: (str(r.get("valid_from") or ""),
                                           str(r.get("recorded_at") or "")), reverse=True)
    parked_legs["temporal"] = leg_payload(
        [{"kind": "fact", "id": r.get("id")} for r in rows if r.get("id")],
        len(page), temporal_limit)
    axis.update({str(r.get("id")): [subject_key(r), axis_key(r)]
                 for r in rows if r.get("id")})
    src.update({str(r.get("id")): str(r.get("episode_id")) for r in rows
                if r.get("id") and r.get("episode_id")})
    # --- the asker's own facts (GH #536) -------------------------------------
    # Gated where the rows arrive, like every other leg, and its axis keys join
    # the same map: a self candidate is projected onto its version chain by
    # `t1-emit` exactly as a keyword-leg candidate is. The store's order is
    # recency (id); since GH #1040 the question re-ranks it (`self_by_query`)
    # unless the old reserved budget is set (`tier1_self_budget` > 0).
    page = bundle_rows(legs_doc, "r-fan-self")
    rows = visible_rows(page)
    if SELF_BUDGET <= 0:
        # GH #1040: ranked by the question, each with its score.
        parked_legs["self"] = leg_payload(
            [{"kind": "fact", "id": r.get("id"), "q": q}
             for r, q in self_by_query(rows, query) if r.get("id")],
            len(page), SELF_LIMIT)
    else:
        parked_legs["self"] = leg_payload(
            [{"kind": "fact", "id": r.get("id")} for r in rows if r.get("id")],
            len(page), SELF_LIMIT)
    axis.update({str(r.get("id")): [subject_key(r), axis_key(r)]
                 for r in rows if r.get("id")})
    src.update({str(r.get("id")): str(r.get("episode_id")) for r in rows
                if r.get("id") and r.get("episode_id")})
    # --- beliefs (tier 2 only) -----------------------------------------------
    # A belief is derived knowledge: its audience_set is the INTERSECTION of the
    # sets of the facts it rests on (contract, Nachtrag 1), written that way by
    # the dreamer. Here it is read like any other tagged row -- with no channel,
    # so the open-history clause cannot reach it.
    b_rows = [r for r in visible_rows(bundle_rows(legs_doc, "r-fan-beliefs"))
              if int(r.get("active", 0) or 0) == 1]
    parked_legs["beliefs"] = [{"id": r.get("id"), "statement": belief_said(r),
                               "confidence": r.get("confidence")} for r in b_rows]
    # --- the active embedding generation -------------------------------------
    m_rows = bundle_rows(legs_doc, "r-fan-model")
    m_row = m_rows[0] if m_rows else {}
    parked_legs["model"] = {"model_id": m_row.get("model_id"), "dim": m_row.get("dim")}
    parked_legs["axis"] = axis
    parked_legs["src"] = src
    emit([park_and_read([("legs", parked_legs)], "t1-park", ["legs", "qvec"])])

if phase == "t1-qvec":
    p = payload_of(d) or {}
    # The REASON travels with the verdict (GH #146). The embed cell states why
    # it gave up (timeout, HTTP status, exhausted retries); dropping it here
    # left the warn line below guessing "no query vector" for every cause
    # there is, which is the one thing an operator cannot act on.
    emit([park_and_read([("qvec", {"vector": p.get("vector"),
                                   "degraded": bool(p.get("degraded")),
                                   "error": p.get("error")})],
                        "t1-qvec-park", ["legs", "qvec"])])

# ----------------------------------------------------------- the rendezvous
if phase in ("t1-park", "t1-qvec-park") and op == "bundle":
    # The ONE place a tier-1 request waits, and the only thing it waits for: the
    # embedder. The store answers in 0-2 ms, the embedder in 0.4-1.0 s, so the
    # vector is always the second half to arrive -- but which half is second is
    # not assumed anywhere, it is READ. Both halves park through the same bundle
    # and read the parking place back in it, and the store runs a bundle's ops in
    # order over its one connection: of two halves parking concurrently exactly
    # ONE reads a complete set (pinned in gh418_a_bundle_sees_its_own_writes.rs).
    # That is what three guarded updates used to buy, one message each.
    legs, worst = parked(d, phase)
    if not {"legs", "qvec"} <= set(legs):
        park()
    if worst > 1:
        sys.stderr.write("recall: rendezvous half parked twice for %s, dropping the echo\n"
                         % rid)
        park()
    store_legs = legs.get("legs") or {}
    qvec = legs.get("qvec") or {}
    anchors = store_legs.get("anchors") or []
    vector = qvec.get("vector")
    model_id = (store_legs.get("model") or {}).get("model_id")
    calls = []
    if anchors:
        calls.append(("r-join-anchor",
                      {"operation": "select", "table": "entities",
                       "columns": ["id", "canonical_name", "subject_key", "kind",
                                   "valid_until"],
                       "where": {"canonical_name": {"in": anchors}}}))
        # GH #1057: the produced entities are keyed by the subject's normal
        # form, so a lower-cased anchor finds them too.
        calls.append(("r-join-anchor-key",
                      {"operation": "select", "table": "entities",
                       "columns": ["id", "canonical_name", "subject_key", "kind",
                                   "valid_until"],
                       "where": {"subject_key": {"in": sorted({a.lower() for a in anchors})}}}))
    # CROSS-MODEL INVARIANT: similar is never called without the active model_id
    # from emb_models. No active generation (or no query vector) means an EMPTY
    # semantic leg -- never an unfiltered ranking across embedding generations.
    if qvec.get("degraded") or not vector or not model_id:
        # Loud, not silent (GH #144): a dead embedder is greppable in the colony
        # log instead of visible only to whoever reads `semantic_degraded`.
        sys.stderr.write("recall: semantic leg skipped, fusing three legs — %s\n" % (
            qvec.get("error") or ("no query vector" if not vector
                                  else "no active embedding model")))
    else:
        # GH #519: BOTH owner kinds, and named rather than left open. An
        # `owner_table` this lane cannot hydrate must not enter the leg -- the
        # audience of a semantic hit is fetched from the owning row, and a row
        # in a table nobody selects reads as the empty set and is dropped
        # silently. So the filter is the list of kinds the hydration below
        # covers, and a future third kind fails to appear rather than failing
        # to be gated.
        calls.append(("r-join-sem",
                      {"operation": "similar", "table": "embeddings",
                       "columns": ["owner_id", "model_id", "owner_table"],
                       "vector_column": "blob", "vector": vector,
                       "where": {"model_id": model_id, "status": "ready",
                                 "owner_table": {"in": list(SEM_OWNER_KIND)}},
                       # GH #691: SEM_FETCH deep, so the fold has something
                       # behind the voting page to move up.
                       "limit": SEM_FETCH}))
    if not calls:
        # No anchors and no vector: two of four legs are empty and the other two
        # are already parked. Nothing is left to ask, so the fusion runs here.
        fuse_and_emit(store_legs, sem=[], sem_aud=[], graph=[])
    emit([store_bundle(calls, "t1-join")])

if phase == "t1-join" and op in ("bundle", "select", "similar"):
    # A bundle is TWO OR MORE tool_calls (`tool_call_turn_count`, store cell.rs):
    # a round with only anchors (dead embedder) or only a vector (no anchors)
    # sends ONE op and gets the classic single-op reply back. Which half it is
    # is not guessed -- the hop names the operation that answered.
    legs_doc = payloads_by_id(d)
    if op == "bundle":
        sem_rows = bundle_rows(legs_doc, "r-join-sem")
        anchor_rows = (bundle_rows(legs_doc, "r-join-anchor")
                       + bundle_rows(legs_doc, "r-join-anchor-key"))
    else:
        sem_rows = rows_of(d) if op == "similar" else []
        anchor_rows = rows_of(d) if op == "select" else []
    # The DISTANCE rides along (#297): this is the only place it exists --
    # `similar` computes it per row and nothing downstream can recompute it --
    # but the scale it is judged against (the model's bit width) lives in another
    # leg, so the number is carried and the verdict is passed at fusion time.
    # The KIND comes off the embedding row (GH #519), it is not assumed: this
    # leg used to be fact-only, and a mislabelled episode would be hydrated out
    # of the wrong table and vanish. A row whose owner kind is not one this
    # lane hydrates is dropped here, at the one place that can still see it.
    sem = [{"kind": SEM_OWNER_KIND[r["owner_table"]], "id": r.get("owner_id"),
            "distance": r.get("distance")}
           for r in sem_rows
           if r.get("owner_id") and r.get("owner_table") in SEM_OWNER_KIND]
    # GH #1057: a hub (the member, whom every question touches) and a closed
    # entity start no walk; a produced entity starts at its subject key, the
    # spelling its edges carry.
    # GH #1057 review (finding 8): at most 32 start, cut by rank -- a name the
    # question spells first -- never alphabetically, or on a large hive the
    # anchor the question names fell out.
    asked = {n.lower() for n in name_anchors(query, []) | set(tokens_of(query))}
    names = sorted({str(r.get("subject_key") or r.get("canonical_name")) for r in anchor_rows
                    if (r.get("subject_key") or r.get("canonical_name"))
                    and r.get("kind") != "hub" and not r.get("valid_until")},
                   key=lambda n: (n.lower() not in asked, n))
    # #280 (item 3): the semantic cap is measured HERE, the only place the page
    # is still whole -- the audience gate of this leg runs at fusion time, and a
    # full page that loses rows there is still a full page.
    calls = [("r-legs-sem",
              {"operation": "insert", "table": "recall_scratch",
               "row": {"request_id": rid, "leg": "sem",
                       "payload": json.dumps(leg_payload(sem, len(sem_rows), SEM_FETCH)),
                       "created_at": now, "fired": 0}})]
    if len(names) > GRAPH_START:
        sys.stderr.write("recall: %d anchor entities, the graph walk starts at the first %d "
                         "(tier1_graph_start)\n" % (len(names), GRAPH_START))
        # GH #1098: parked beside the semantic leg, so the fusion names the cut
        # in the bundle (`graph_cuts`) whichever hop it runs in.
        calls.append(("r-legs-start-cut",
                      {"operation": "insert", "table": "recall_scratch",
                       "row": {"request_id": rid, "leg": "start-cut",
                               "payload": json.dumps([GRAPH_START, len(names)]),
                               "created_at": now, "fired": 0}}))
    if names:
        calls.append(("r-legs-graph",
                      {"operation": "traverse", "table": "entity_edges",
                       "src": "src_entity", "dst": "dst_entity", "kind": "edge_kind",
                       "weight": "weight",
                       "columns": ["episode_id", "channel", "audience_set", "relation"],
                       # GH #1057: never INTO a hub -- its neighbours are everyone.
                       "start": names[:GRAPH_START], "where": {"valid_until": {"is_null": True},
                                                      "edge_kind": {"or_null": {"neq": "co-hub"}}},
                       "max_depth": GRAPH_DEPTH, "max_nodes": GRAPH_NODES}))
    ids = [c["id"] for c in sem if c["kind"] == "fact"]
    sem_ep_ids = [c["id"] for c in sem if c["kind"] == "episode"]
    if sem_ep_ids:
        # The episode half of the same problem: an episode row carries its own
        # channel and audience_set, so the gate has everything it needs. No axis
        # keys: an episode has no subject/predicate axis, and `fuse_and_emit`
        # reads the axis map for fact candidates only. GH #691: plus what the
        # fold reads -- the content's normal form and the recency that picks
        # the representative (`fold_episodes`, `episode_ord`).
        calls.append(("r-legs-sem-aud-ep",
                      {"operation": "select", "table": "episodes",
                       "columns": ["id", "channel", "audience_set", "content",
                                   "happened_at", "recorded_at", "closure_source", "muted_at", "unmuted_at", "mute_words", "speaker_name"],
                       "where": {"id": {"in": sem_ep_ids}}, "limit": SEM_FETCH}))
    if ids:
        # The ONE leg whose rows are not the tagged rows themselves: `similar`
        # ranks EMBEDDINGS, and the embeddings table carries no participant set.
        # So the audience of the OWNING facts is fetched here -- and their
        # canonical axis keys with it, so the axis page can ride in the hydration
        # bundle rather than one hop behind it (#418).
        calls.append(("r-legs-sem-aud",
                      {"operation": "select", "table": "facts",
                       "columns": ["id", "channel", "audience_set",
                                   "canonical_subject", "canonical_predicate",
                                   "subject", "predicate", "episode_id", "closure_source", "muted_at", "unmuted_at", "mute_words"],
                       "where": {"id": {"in": ids}}, "limit": SEM_FETCH}))
    calls.append(("r-legs-read",
                  {"operation": "select", "table": "recall_scratch",
                   "columns": ["request_id", "leg", "payload", "fired"],
                   "where": {"request_id": rid, "leg": {"in": ["legs", "sem", "start-cut"]}}}))
    emit([store_bundle(calls, "t1-legs")])

if phase == "t1-legs" and op == "bundle":
    legs_doc = payloads_by_id(d)
    parked_legs, worst = legs_from(bundle_rows(legs_doc, "r-legs-read"))
    if "legs" not in parked_legs:
        park()
    if worst > 1:
        sys.stderr.write("recall: legs parked twice for %s, dropping the echo\n" % rid)
        park()
    store_legs = parked_legs.get("legs") or {}
    sem = leg_hits(parked_legs.get("sem"))
    sem_leg = parked_legs.get("sem")
    start_cut = parked_legs.get("start-cut") or None
    sem_aud_rows = (bundle_rows(legs_doc, "r-legs-sem-aud")
                    + bundle_rows(legs_doc, "r-legs-sem-aud-ep"))
    # --- the graph leg, word for word what `t1-graph` computed ---------------
    p = payload_of_bundle_leg(legs_doc, "r-legs-graph")
    paths = (p or {}).get("paths", []) if isinstance(p, dict) else []
    # The gate ON THE EDGE (contract, Nachtrag 1). `entity_edges` inherit channel
    # and audience_set from the episode they were extracted from, and `traverse`
    # projects the attributes of the LAST edge of each path -- which is exactly
    # the edge whose episode_id becomes the candidate below. So the graph leg
    # gates its own rows here, before its ranking and therefore before fusion.
    # A depth-0 anchor row carries NULL attributes, reads as the empty set and
    # drops out; it carries no episode_id either, so nothing is lost.
    page_paths = len(paths)
    # GH #1057 review (finding 5): once edges exist the LAST edge is not
    # enough -- a path is kept only when every edge on it passed the gate.
    paths = gate_paths(paths)
    # Rank by (depth asc, weight_sum desc, node asc). The walk yields TWO kinds
    # (GH #520): the EPISODE the edge carries as its provenance, and the FACTS
    # the NODE is about -- and the second half needs one more bundle, because
    # the nodes a walk passed through are only known AFTER the walk, and the
    # walk's reply is this hop.
    # GH #1057: ranked where the question's parts meet (`rank_walk`); without
    # anchor ranks and relations this is the old (depth, weight, node) order.
    paths = rank_walk(paths, store_legs.get("anchor_rank") or {}, query)
    # The walk, folded down to the two things the leg is built from: the node in
    # `facts.canonical_subject` normalisation and the edge's episode id, in rank
    # order. Parked rather than recomputed, because a traverse cannot be asked
    # twice for the same page without paying for it twice.
    # Fix round 3: the names the walk touched ride along -- they are no
    # question words, neither for an edge's relation nor for a node's facts.
    names = sorted({str(n).strip().lower() for r in paths for n in (r.get("path") or []) if n})
    # ... and per node the question words its edges carry, plus the nodes the
    # question itself names (anchor rank 0): their facts need no edge.
    anchor_rank = store_legs.get("anchor_rank") or {}
    # A node whose edges carry no relation (a graph from before #1057) gets no
    # entry and keeps the old behaviour.
    via = {}
    for r in paths:
        relation = (r.get("edge") or {}).get("relation")
        if relation:
            via.setdefault(node_key(r.get("node")), set()).update(edge_words(relation, names))
    walk = {"page_paths": page_paths, "names": names, "start_cut": start_cut,
            "via": {k: sorted(v) for k, v in via.items()},
            # named = the whole name or one of its words (len >= 3) is a
            # question anchor of rank 0: "my friend Gustav" names gustav raschke.
            "asked": sorted(n for n in names if anchor_rank.get(n) == 0 or any(
                len(t) >= 3 and anchor_rank.get(t) == 0 for t in n.split())),
            "seq": [[node_key(r.get("node")), (r.get("edge") or {}).get("episode_id"),
                     edge_rel((r.get("edge") or {}).get("relation"), names)]
                    for r in paths]}
    nodes = []
    for n, *_edge in walk["seq"]:
        if n and n not in nodes:
            nodes.append(n)
    walk["fact_nodes"] = len(nodes)
    if nodes:
        # The seventh store message of a tier-1 recall, and the ONLY one that is
        # conditional (#418 counts six): a request with no anchors, or one whose
        # walk came back empty, fuses right here for six exactly as before. What
        # the message buys is the leg's whole point -- a fact about an entity the
        # QUESTION never named, reached over an edge.
        emit([store_bundle(
            [("r-graph-walk",
              {"operation": "insert", "table": "recall_scratch",
               "row": {"request_id": rid, "leg": "graph-walk",
                       "payload": json.dumps(walk), "created_at": now, "fired": 0}}),
             # The semantic companion rides along: it arrived in THIS reply and
             # the fusion now runs one hop later, so it has to be parked or it
             # would have to be selected a second time.
             ("r-graph-sem-aud",
              {"operation": "insert", "table": "recall_scratch",
               "row": {"request_id": rid, "leg": "sem-aud",
                       "payload": json.dumps(sem_aud_rows), "created_at": now,
                       "fired": 0}}),
            ] + [
             # GH #1057: ONE page per walked node, newest first. One page over all
             # nodes (`limit` 100, store order) came back oldest first: measured on a
             # 6-month history, 129-174 facts on the reached nodes and the current
             # value at position 105-137, cut before any ranking could see it.
             ("r-graph-fact-%d" % i,
              {"operation": "select", "table": "facts",
               # The two canonical columns are what the fusion's axis map needs
               # (see `fuse_and_emit`); the two written ones are its documented
               # fallback for a row from before the canonical migration.
               "columns": ["id", "subject", "canonical_subject", "predicate",
                           "canonical_predicate", "channel", "audience_set",
                           "episode_id", "closure_source", "muted_at", "unmuted_at", "mute_words", "claim", "valid_from",
                           # fix round 3: who said it -- first hand before hearsay
                           "source"],
               # R1, one line: no `expired_at` and no `superseded_by` in the
               # where clause -- the version chain is the truth and the cache
               # columns are not consulted. A superseded hit is not dropped
               # here, `t1-emit` projects it onto its successor exactly as it
               # does for a keyword-leg fact.
               "where": {"canonical_subject": node},
               "order_by": [{"col": "valid_from", "dir": "desc"}],
               "limit": GRAPH_NODE_PAGE})
             for i, node in enumerate(nodes[:GRAPH_FACT_PAGES])] + [
             ("r-graph-read",
              {"operation": "select", "table": "recall_scratch",
               "columns": ["request_id", "leg", "payload", "fired"],
               "where": {"request_id": rid,
                         "leg": {"in": ["legs", "sem", "graph-walk", "sem-aud"]}}})],
            "t1-graph")])
    fuse_and_emit(store_legs, sem=sem_leg, sem_aud=sem_aud_rows,
                  graph=graph_leg_of(walk, []), start_cut=start_cut)


if phase == "t1-graph" and op == "bundle":
    # GH #520: the join the walk was one bundle short of. `entity_edges` carries
    # `episode_id` as its provenance -- that half was always true -- but its
    # node names are NOT a namespace of their own: they are
    # `facts.canonical_subject` in the written spelling. So the leg was never
    # blocked by the schema, it stopped one join short, and this is the join.
    #
    # Everything the fusion needs is read back HERE -- the parked fan, the
    # semantic leg, its companion page and the walk -- so the fusion runs in
    # this hop, and `t1-legs` fuses only when there was nothing to join.
    legs_doc = payloads_by_id(d)
    parked_legs, worst = legs_from(bundle_rows(legs_doc, "r-graph-read"))
    if "legs" not in parked_legs or "graph-walk" not in parked_legs:
        park()
    if worst > 1:
        sys.stderr.write("recall: graph walk parked twice for %s, dropping the echo\n" % rid)
        park()
    fact_rows = [r for cid in sorted(legs_doc, key=lambda c: (len(c), c))
                 if cid.startswith("r-graph-fact") for r in bundle_rows(legs_doc, cid)]
    fuse_and_emit(parked_legs.get("legs") or {}, sem=parked_legs.get("sem"),
                  sem_aud=parked_legs.get("sem-aud") or [],
                  graph=graph_leg_of(parked_legs.get("graph-walk") or {}, fact_rows),
                  graph_facts=[r for r in fact_rows
                               if isinstance(r, dict) and visible_row(r)],
                  start_cut=(parked_legs.get("graph-walk") or {}).get("start_cut"))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- RRF fusion

# ----------------------------------------------------------------- emit / t2
if phase == "t1-emit" and op in ("bundle", "select") and not err:
    if op == "bundle":
        # #418: everything this phase reads arrived in ONE reply -- the parked
        # legs through the trailing select, the axis page and the cardinality
        # verdicts as legs of the same bundle. The `else` branch below is the
        # tier-2 downgrade, which still comes in over a single-op select.
        legs_doc = payloads_by_id(d)
        legs, _worst = legs_from(bundle_rows(legs_doc, "r-hyd-read"))
        # Residual guard, the argument the two hydration phases carried: these
        # ids come from an already gated ranking, so this drops nothing in a
        # healthy run -- and a candidate without a hydration row is dropped below
        # anyway, which makes the guard cost one comparison and close the path if
        # a leg ever forgets its gate.
        facts = {str(r.get("id")): r
                 for r in visible_rows(bundle_rows(legs_doc, "r-hyd-fact"))}
        episodes = {str(r.get("id")): r
                    for r in visible_rows(bundle_rows(legs_doc, "r-hyd-ep"))}
        # NOT a residual guard (R8, Nachtrag 3) -- this is a real hole otherwise.
        # The axis page is a CROSS PRODUCT over canonical subject x predicate: it
        # deliberately returns facts no leg ever hit, and `project_fact_candidate`
        # projects a superseded candidate onto its SUCCESSOR out of exactly these
        # rows. An ungated axis would therefore render a claim this round may not
        # see, through a candidate it may.
        #
        # R7 (Nachtrag 3): and this is where the chain BREAKS. Removing a version
        # before the chain is built is the right order -- the other way round the
        # existence of an invisible version would show through the validity span,
        # and asking often enough maps out when something was said in a room one
        # is not in. But the price must not be paid silently: without the mark
        # below a claim whose successor is invisible renders as current, and the
        # agent answers wrong. So the surviving rows of a broken axis carry one
        # boolean.
        axis_page, lost_axes = [], set()
        for r in bundle_rows(legs_doc, "r-hyd-axis"):
            if not isinstance(r, dict):
                continue
            if visible_row(r):
                axis_page.append(r)
            else:
                lost_axes.add((subject_key(r), axis_key(r)))
        for r in axis_page:
            if (subject_key(r), axis_key(r)) in lost_axes:
                # The flag rides on the ROW so that it reaches every consumer of
                # the axis page at once (project_fact_candidate, fact_span,
                # superseded_marker). A candidate gets it because its AXIS is
                # marked, not because some row it was built from carried a key.
                r["supersession_unknown"] = True
        # The MAP the projection consumes, not the rows: one shape, derived once,
        # so the read path cannot disagree with itself between two requests. A
        # store too old to carry the table answers with an error outcome and the
        # map stays empty, which is the pre-W5 behaviour exactly.
        judged_map = {}
        for r in bundle_rows(legs_doc, "r-hyd-card"):
            if not isinstance(r, dict):
                continue
            key = str(r.get("canonical_predicate") or "")
            verdict = str(r.get("verdict") or "")
            if key and verdict in ("single", "multi"):
                judged_map[key] = verdict
        legs["hyd-axis"] = axis_page
        legs["card"] = judged_map
        # GH #936: the marks of the fact hits' source episodes, by episode id --
        # only of episodes this round may read. A fact visible through a wider
        # set than its episode reads as UNMARKED: the filter drops it whatever
        # the mark says, so neither the record nor the hit set carries a bit
        # about a turn the round could not see.
        marks = {str(r.get("id")): parse_mark(r.get("affect"))
                 for r in visible_rows(bundle_rows(legs_doc, "r-hyd-affect"))
                 if isinstance(r, dict) and r.get("id")}
    else:
        legs = by_leg(d)
        facts = {str(r.get("id")): r for r in (legs.get("hyd-fact") or [])}
        episodes = {str(r.get("id")): r for r in (legs.get("hyd-ep") or [])}
        marks = {}
    # The axis rows are trimmed to the read instant BEFORE the chain is built:
    # "current" means current AS OF the request (spec D.5), never "newest on
    # disk" -- otherwise a question about the past would be answered with a fact
    # that was not written yet at that time.
    axis_rows = [r for r in (legs.get("hyd-axis") or [])
                 if str(r.get("valid_from") or "") <= as_of]
    # R7 (Nachtrag 3): the axes whose version chain lost a row to the gate. Read
    # from the UNTRIMMED leg on purpose -- a version newer than the read instant
    # is trimmed out one line above, and a version newer than the read instant is
    # exactly the kind that makes a survivor's currency unvouchable.
    unknown_axes = {(subject_key(r), axis_key(r))
                    for r in (legs.get("hyd-axis") or [])
                    if isinstance(r, dict) and r.get("supersession_unknown")}
    # W5 (#13, ruling Q3): the store's judged cardinality, one map from relation
    # to verdict. A bundle whose leg is empty reads exactly as it read before --
    # the seed list and the session-guarded rule are still underneath.
    judged = legs.get("card") or {}
    if not isinstance(judged, dict):
        judged = {}
    fused = legs.get("fused") or {}
    # The window is read again here rather than carried on the leg payload: the
    # context slot is persistent, so every phase of one request sees the same
    # answer, and the fused ranking keeps its shape (kind, id, score, legs).
    window = read_window(ctx)
    # seen_facts maps a projected fact id onto the SLOT its survivor occupies, so a
    # later hit on the same axis can still hand over its legs (O-4b).
    candidates, spent, seen_facts, win_ord = [], 0, {}, {}
    # #280 (item 3): whether the budget ended the list is known HERE and nowhere
    # else -- one line further down the loop has already left.
    cut_by_budget = False
    # #15: seen_eps maps the NORMAL FORM of an episode onto the slot its line
    # occupies, ep_newest onto the recency of the copy currently rendered there.
    seen_eps, ep_newest = {}, {}
    # GH #691: the copies each line stands for -- a SET, because a query leg may
    # already have folded copies into one candidate (`copies`), and two legs
    # may have folded the same copy onto different representatives.
    ep_copies = {}
    for c in fused.get("candidates") or []:
        row = facts.get(str(c["id"])) if c["kind"] == "fact" else episodes.get(str(c["id"]))
        if row is None:
            continue
        ord_key = None
        if c["kind"] == "fact":
            # R4: in a POINT query the candidate is the CURRENT fact of the
            # hit's axis; a superseded hit turns into a history entry on its
            # successor. A WINDOW query does NOT collapse: R4 exists so that a
            # superseded claim never looks like the truth in force, and in an
            # explicit time-range question the versions themselves are the
            # answer -- each carrying the span it was valid for. The fallback
            # keeps a candidate WITHOUT history rather than losing it when the
            # axis select was truncated or carried no matching pair.
            if window is None:
                row = project_fact_candidate(str(c["id"]), axis_rows, judged) or dict(
                    row, history=[])
            else:
                # The fallback reads the CLOSURE, exactly as the item below
                # does and as `span_end` does: a materialised closure lives in
                # `expired_at`, not in `valid_until`, and the raw column made a
                # closed statement render `[2026-01-01 -> open]` next to its own
                # `valid_until` naming the day it ended. The third source of
                # `span_end` (the next re-assertion) is deliberately absent --
                # it is derived from the axis page, and the axis page is exactly
                # what was truncated when this branch runs.
                row = fact_span(str(c["id"]), axis_rows) or dict(
                    row, history=[],
                    span={"from": row.get("valid_from"),
                          "until": row.get("valid_until") or row.get("expired_at") or None})
            # GH #936: the filter decides on the row that will be RENDERED (the
            # projection above), after the gate and before it takes a slot.
            mark = marks.get(str(row.get("episode_id") or ""))
            if not affect_pass(affect_filter, mark):
                continue
            # Two hits on one axis collapse into one candidate. First wins: the
            # fusion order is already total (score, best_rank, leg, kind, id),
            # so which hit survives is deterministic.
            if str(row.get("id")) in seen_facts:
                # O-4b: the hit is dropped, its ATTRIBUTION is not.
                merge_legs(candidates[seen_facts[str(row.get("id"))]], c["legs"])
                continue
            # The slot this candidate will occupy once it clears the budget check --
            # same idiom as win_ord below. A candidate that breaks the budget ends the
            # loop, so the recorded slot is never read without being filled.
            seen_facts[str(row.get("id"))] = len(candidates)
            if window is not None:
                ord_key = ((row.get("valid_from") or ""),
                           (row.get("recorded_at") or ""),
                           str(row.get("id") or ""))
        else:
            # #15: a question asked five times is ONE line with a count, not five
            # slots holding one string. Same first-winner semantics as the axis
            # collapse above -- the best-ranked copy owns the slot and collects the
            # legs of the copies that fold into it (O-4b) -- and the same
            # PRESENTATION-only scope: no row is touched, level 0 stays
            # append-only, the collapse lives in the bundle and nowhere else. An
            # empty normal form is no identity at all, so it never collapses.
            mark = parse_mark(row.get("affect"))
            if not affect_pass(affect_filter, mark):
                continue
            key = normalize_text(row.get("content"))
            slot = seen_eps.get(key) if key else None
            mine_copies = set(str(i) for i in (c.get("copies") or [c["id"]]))
            if slot is not None:
                merge_legs(candidates[slot], c["legs"])
                ep_copies[key] |= mine_copies
                candidates[slot]["seen"] = len(ep_copies[key])
                if episode_ord(row) > ep_newest[key]:
                    ep_newest[key] = episode_ord(row)
                    adopt_episode(candidates[slot], c["id"], row)
                continue
            if key:
                # The slot this line will occupy once it clears the budget check --
                # same idiom as seen_facts above.
                seen_eps[key] = len(candidates)
                ep_newest[key] = episode_ord(row)
                ep_copies[key] = mine_copies
        item = {"rank": len(candidates) + 1, "kind": c["kind"], "id": c["id"],
                "score": c["score"], "legs": c["legs"],
                # Q8: the vote count behind that score, carried onto the record
                # so the trace can say WHY one candidate outranks another. NOT
                # merged on a collapse: score and rank are the first winner's
                # (O-4b), and a count that no longer matched the score beside it
                # would describe a fusion that never happened.
                "agreement": c.get("agreement", 1),
                # The record always says it, null = unknown (GH #936).
                "affect": mark}
        if c["kind"] == "fact":
            item["id"] = row.get("id")
            item["history"] = row.get("history") or []
            # W1 (ruling Q6). The key is absent when nothing closed the
            # statement, so only a superseded candidate pays a byte of budget for
            # it, and the ranking is untouched -- the demotion of closed
            # statements is its own package.
            marker = superseded_marker(row, axis_rows, as_of)
            if marker is not None:
                item["superseded"] = str(marker or "")
            if window is not None:
                item["span"] = row.get("span")
            item["text"] = str(said_of(row) or "")
            # GH #849: who said it travels as a key of its own too, absent for the
            # member's own side, so the JSON beside the text carries the same
            # attribution the text does.
            if str(row.get("source") or ""):
                item["source"] = str(row.get("source"))
            # GH #67: `foresight` is the statement-level intention marker, and
            # since a speech act may not be a predicate any more it is the only
            # thing left that tells a plan from a fact on a shared axis. Absent
            # for the other two kinds, exactly like the currency marker above, so
            # a world candidate pays no byte of budget for it.
            if str(row.get("fact_kind") or "") == "foresight":
                item["intent"] = "planned"
            # R7 (Nachtrag 3): this candidate's axis lost a version to the
            # audience gate, so no currency may be asserted for it. ONE boolean
            # and nothing else -- not the count, not the instant, not the channel
            # of what was removed, because any of those would rebuild the side
            # channel in a finer grain. What the asker learns is only: I know
            # this, and I cannot vouch that it still holds. That is a statement
            # about this agent's certainty, not about the other room. Absent
            # unless true, so an unaffected candidate costs no byte of budget and
            # renders byte for byte as before.
            if (subject_key(row), axis_key(row)) in unknown_axes:
                item["supersession_unknown"] = True
            item["subject"] = row.get("subject")
            item["predicate"] = row.get("predicate")
            item["valid_from"] = row.get("valid_from")
            # #280 (item 4): validity used to travel in one direction only -- the
            # bundle carried the DERIVED currency marker and threw away the two
            # columns the store answers with. `valid_until` is unconditional
            # because `null` is the honest "still open" and an absent key would be
            # a different claim; `superseded_by` is absent unless a successor was
            # actually named, because there is nothing to say when nobody replaced
            # the statement. The marker above stays exactly as it is -- this only
            # stops the store's own answer from being dropped next to it.
            #
            # The value is the CLOSURE, not the raw column, and it MIRRORS
            # `span_end`: a statement that says when it stops being true says it
            # about itself, and across statement boundaries a materialised closure
            # (`expired_at`) says it instead. Reading only the raw column made a
            # closed fact read as open next to its own `superseded_by`, its own
            # `span` and its own currency marker -- three fields of one candidate
            # contradicting each other about the same closure. What is NOT read
            # here is the third source of `span_end` (the next re-assertion): that
            # one is derived from the axis page, it is not the store's answer
            # about this row, and `span` already renders it in window mode.
            item["valid_until"] = row.get("valid_until") or row.get("expired_at") or None
            if str(row.get("superseded_by") or "").strip():
                item["superseded_by"] = row.get("superseded_by")
            # #280 (item 1): the store keeps a `confidence` on every fact, the
            # hydration selects it and the axis page selects it again -- and this
            # branch was where it stopped. Without it a reader has to treat a
            # hedged statement and a certain one as the same claim. Absent unless
            # the column holds a number, same discipline as `intent` and
            # `supersession_unknown` above: a candidate that knows nothing pays no
            # byte of the budget for saying so.
            conf = row.get("confidence")
            if conf is not None and conf != "":
                try:
                    item["confidence"] = int(conf)
                except (TypeError, ValueError):
                    pass
            item["episode_id"] = row.get("episode_id")
            # #148: a fact knows which session it was said in -- the column is
            # selected, the episode branch keeps it, and this branch used to
            # drop it. Without it a fact cannot be grouped with the turn it came
            # from, and a question that spans sessions has to be answered from a
            # list that no longer knows what a session is.
            item["session_id"] = row.get("session_id")
        else:
            item["text"] = str(row.get("content") or "")
            item["sender"] = said_by(row)
            item["session_id"] = row.get("session_id")
            item["happened_at"] = row.get("happened_at")
            # GH #691: a candidate a query leg folded already stands for its copies.
            item["seen"] = max(1, len(c.get("copies") or []))
        # #296: the budget measures what TRAVELS. The record is the trace's
        # copy and the trace pays no prompt budget, so costing it would spend
        # the whole saving on filling the budget with more rows instead of
        # shipping a smaller bundle -- TOPK stays the count cap, this line is
        # the size cap, and it has to weigh the same thing the model reads.
        def cost1(x):
            return estimate_tokens(payload_candidate(x))
        cost = cost1(item)
        # Hard budget cut: the FIRST item that does not fit ends the loop, so the
        # output stays a pure prefix of the ranking. GH #1085: an item that does
        # not fit the bundle even on its own is cut to what is left, with its
        # mark, and ends the list -- before, a 400-character cap per item kept
        # it small; an empty bundle for one long first fact would be worse.
        if spent + cost > T1_TOKENS:
            cut_by_budget = True
            fitted = (fit_text(item, "text", T1_TOKENS - spent, cost1)
                      if cost > T1_TOKENS else None)
            if fitted is None:
                break
            item, cost = fitted, cost1(fitted)
        if ord_key is not None:
            win_ord[len(candidates)] = ord_key
        candidates.append(item)
        spent += cost
        if cut_by_budget:
            break
    if window is not None and win_ord:
        # O-2: in window mode the temporal ordering IS the answer (Task 5 / R5),
        # so it binds -- RRF picks the candidates, it does not order them. Only
        # the fact slots are permuted, episodes keep theirs, and the output stays
        # a pure prefix of the ranking. Two passes because the direction differs
        # per component: id ascending, then valid_from/recorded_at descending.
        slots = sorted(win_ord)
        pairs = [(win_ord[i], candidates[i]) for i in slots]
        pairs.sort(key=lambda p: p[0][2])
        pairs.sort(key=lambda p: (p[0][0], p[0][1]), reverse=True)
        for slot, pair in zip(slots, pairs):
            candidates[slot] = pair[1]
    for i, cand in enumerate(candidates):
        cand["rank"] = i + 1
    # GH #936: beliefs carry no mark, so a set filter keeps none.
    beliefs = [] if affect_filter is not None else (legs.get("beliefs") or [])
    # #280 (item 3): only the producer knows whether this list is the whole
    # answer. Twenty candidates read the same whether twenty was all there was or
    # all that fit, and a question that counts is answered wrong off a prefix
    # nobody declared as one. Three cuts can shorten the list, and each is read
    # off the place it actually happened: the leg caps off the PAGES that
    # reported them (`leg_capped`, never the summed and gated `leg_sizes` -- that
    # sum is a different question and answers this one wrong in both
    # directions), the fusion cut off the fused list, the budget off the loop
    # above. Nothing is measured twice and nothing is re-derived from a total.
    caps = fused.get("leg_capped") or {}
    # Q8: only a leg that VOTES can have cost this list a row. A zero-weight leg
    # nominates nothing (fuse_rank), so its full page cannot have shortened the
    # answer, and reading it as a cut hedges a bundle nothing was taken from --
    # in point mode the temporal leg comes back at its limit almost every time.
    # The mode is read from the same `fusion_weights` that fused the run, so the
    # two cannot disagree. The raw flags stay in `leg_capped` for the diagnostic:
    # what a page reported is a fact about the RUN either way, and only its
    # reading as a cut in the ANSWER is mode-dependent.
    voting = fusion_weights(ctx)
    capped_legs = [n for n in LEG_ORDER if caps.get(n) and voting[n] > 0]
    cut_by_topk = len(fused.get("candidates") or []) >= TOPK
    cuts = []
    if capped_legs:
        # "possibly", because an exactly-full page is ambiguous by construction:
        # the store answers with rows, never with "and there are more".
        cuts.append("capped legs (possibly more exist): "
                    + ", ".join("%s at %d rows" % (n, int(caps[n]))
                                for n in capped_legs))
    if cut_by_topk:
        cuts.append("the fusion cut at TOPK=%d" % TOPK)
    # GH #1098: an entity the graph walk never reached is a cut like any other.
    graph_cuts = fused.get("graph_cuts") or {}
    if graph_cuts.get("anchors"):
        cuts.append("the entity join looked up %d of %d name anchors (tier1_graph_anchors)"
                    % tuple(graph_cuts["anchors"]))
    if graph_cuts.get("start"):
        cuts.append("the graph walk started at %d of %d anchor entities (tier1_graph_start)"
                    % tuple(graph_cuts["start"]))
    if cut_by_budget:
        cuts.append("the token budget of %d ended the list at %d candidates"
                    % (T1_TOKENS, len(candidates)))
    legs_present = fused.get("legs_present", [])
    # #296: the PAYLOAD half. What travels is what answers the question --
    # the claim, the axis it sits on, when it started and, when the store said
    # so, when it stopped. The row ids, the fused scores, the ranks, the legs,
    # the sessions and the full version chains are retrieval bookkeeping (the
    # list of #279): they cost prompt budget, they invite a model to reason
    # about a score it cannot interpret, and they are all one slot over in
    # `recall_diagnostic`. `legs_present`, `leg_sizes` and `semantic_degraded`
    # leave for the same reason and to the same place -- they describe the RUN,
    # never the answer.
    bundle = {"query": query, "tier": int(tier), "as_of": as_of,
              # Q8 (#297): the bundle's verdict on itself. A caller that has
              # to branch on "did memory answer this" had to measure the
              # candidate list and then guess what an empty one meant -- a
              # store with nothing in it, a floor that removed everything, or
              # a run that failed. One word says it, and the rendered half
              # below says the same thing to the model that reads text.
              "answers": "direct" if candidates else "none",
              "candidates": [payload_candidate(c) for c in candidates],
              "beliefs": beliefs,
              "complete": not cuts,
              "token_estimate": spent}
    # Absent when nothing was cut -- a complete bundle has no cut to name, and
    # the same absent-unless-known discipline the candidate keys follow.
    if cuts:
        bundle["complete_reason"] = "; ".join(cuts)
    # #88: same verdict, one tier up -- and here it is also RENDERED, because
    # at tier 1 the candidate list itself is what the clamp shaped, and the
    # model reads the text rather than the JSON beside it (same argument as
    # window_ignored at tier 0).
    if query_hygiene is not None:
        bundle["query_hygiene"] = query_hygiene
    # #279: the opening line ASSERTS. It used to name the RUN -- how many
    # candidates, fused by RRF over which legs -- and a model told it holds 3 of
    # N ranked hits reads every row under it as a maybe. Measured on a live
    # agent: same store, same fact, same channel, only this framing changed, and
    # the answer was "not reliably known" about a statement the model had read
    # and attributed correctly. It was not ignoring the bundle; it was believing
    # what the bundle said about itself. The line now says what the document IS
    # and as of when -- the one piece of framing a reader can use -- and it was
    # also the last place a leg name reached this text (#281 took them out of
    # the rows). The run's own description is not gone: it is the first line of
    # `recall_diagnostic["text"]`, unchanged.
    #
    # Q8 (#297): unless there is nothing to assert. The header is a promise
    # that something follows it -- the same argument `render_payload_lines`
    # makes about an empty section, one level up -- and over no rows it is a
    # promise the document does not keep.
    if candidates:
        lines = ["WHAT THIS MEMORY HOLDS (as of %s)" % fmt_day(as_of)]
    else:
        lines = [empty_state_sentence(as_of, fused)]
    # #88, re-worded (#279): the hygiene verdict is the one piece of bookkeeping
    # that IS payload -- it says the question this was looked up with is not the
    # question that was asked, which is a statement about THIS answer's
    # reliability and not about the machinery. So it stays, in words: no key
    # name, no leg, nothing a reader has to decode first. The step, the counts
    # and the verdict itself still travel in the JSON, on the header and in the
    # record, which is where a caller reads them.
    if query_hygiene is not None:
        lines.append("The question was shortened before this was looked up "
                     "(%d -> %d characters) -- an answer to what was dropped "
                     "may be missing here."
                     % (query_hygiene["from_chars"], query_hygiene["to_chars"]))
    # #280, rendered (#279): the same argument one field over. Only the producer
    # knows whether this list is the whole answer, and a `complete` flag is
    # useless to a model that never reads the JSON beside the text -- a list cut
    # short reads as the whole answer, which is the wrong answer to every
    # question that counts. The reason is the SAME string the bundle carries:
    # two halves of one message describing the same cut differently would be
    # worse than either of them alone. It names the leg a cap ended, and that is
    # the one sentence in this text written FOR the reader in which a leg name
    # earns its place -- "possibly more exist" is what a reader has to know.
    # Above the rows, where a reader meets it before reading what it qualifies.
    #
    # Q8 (#297): and not at all when there is no list. "Not everything that
    # matches is here" qualifies ROWS -- under a sentence that says nothing
    # matched, it is a hedge about a list that does not exist, and it invites
    # exactly the "there must be more, answer from somewhere else" reading the
    # empty state was built to close. What the empty case has to say about
    # completeness, it says in its own sentence: hits came back and none
    # cleared the floor. The cut itself is NOT lost -- `complete` and
    # `complete_reason` stay in the bundle JSON and the caps stay in
    # `recall_diagnostic`, so nothing becomes harder to debug (#296).
    if candidates and not bundle["complete"]:
        lines.append("Not everything that matches is here -- %s."
                     % bundle["complete_reason"])
    # #281: two sections, one per kind. `render_candidate_line` keeps every byte
    # of its output and IS the diagnostic renderer since #279 -- the leg names,
    # the bracket and the flat ranking are what explains a retrieval afterwards,
    # and they are the wrong text to hand a model that has to answer a question.
    lines.extend(render_payload_lines(candidates))
    # #296 (precondition): two audiences, two slots. `system.memory.bundle` is
    # the PAYLOAD -- what the model reads, and what the rest of this package
    # trims down. This is the RECORD: the candidate list exactly as the loop
    # built it, next to the bookkeeping of the run those numbers only mean
    # something against. It is a top-level body slot, NOT `system` and NOT a
    # message, so the collector's `in_bundle` lane -- which keeps `system` and
    # `messages` and nothing else -- drops it, while the message log keeps the
    # whole body. The trace therefore survives without ever reaching the next
    # prompt. Precedent for a cell-specific top-level slot: `close_batch` in
    # the collector's `assemble`, which hands `rounds` over the same way.
    #
    # The trace keeps EVERYTHING, and that is precisely why the later packages
    # of #296 may take fields out of the payload: nothing becomes harder to
    # debug, because whatever leaves the bundle is still here.
    diagnostic = {"as_of": as_of, "query": query, "tier": int(tier),
                  "recall_id": rid,
                  # #279: the readable form the payload gave up, byte for byte.
                  # Whoever has to explain an answer needs the flat ranking and
                  # the leg tags in the shape they always had -- reconstructing
                  # them from the record is work, and work nobody does is a
                  # trace nobody reads.
                  "text": render_diagnostic_text(candidates, fused, 1),
                  "legs_present": legs_present,
                  "leg_sizes": fused.get("leg_sizes", {}),
                  "leg_sizes_raw": fused.get("leg_sizes_raw", {}),
                  "leg_capped": fused.get("leg_capped", {}),
                  "semantic_degraded": bool(fused.get("semantic_degraded", True)),
                  "candidates": candidates}
    header = {"route": "bundle", "recall_id": rid}
    if query_hygiene is not None:
        header["query_hygiene"] = query_hygiene["step"]
    if not candidates:
        # Q8 (#297): absent unless true, like every other marker on this
        # header. A router that has to branch on "memory had nothing" reads
        # one key instead of parsing the bundle it was handed on.
        header["recall_empty"] = "1"
    if tier == "2" and phase == "t1-emit":
        # #418: the rendered bundle travels as ONE parked row BESIDE the
        # dialectic request, so a provider error has a single row to read back
        # instead of five legs to project a second time. The seventh store
        # message of a tier-2 request is this one, and it is not on the critical
        # path: it leaves together with the provider call, never before it.
        emit([{"header": {"route": "dialectic", "phase": "dialectic", "recall_id": rid},
               "system": {"instructions": {"text": DIALECTIC_PROMPT}},
               "messages": [{"origin": "user", "type": "text",
                             # #148: `sessions` travels WITH the flat list, not
                             # instead of it. The ranking is still the best
                             # answer to "what is most relevant"; the grouping
                             # is the answer to "what belongs together". A
                             # question that spans sessions needs the second one
                             # and used to get only the first.
                             "text": json.dumps({"question": query, "as_of": as_of,
                                                 "beliefs": beliefs,
                                                 "sessions": sessions_view(candidates),
                                                 "candidates": candidates}, sort_keys=True)}]},
              store_op({"operation": "insert", "table": "recall_scratch",
                        "row": {"request_id": rid, "leg": "rendered",
                                "payload": json.dumps({"bundle": bundle, "lines": lines,
                                                       "diagnostic": diagnostic}),
                                "created_at": now, "fired": 0}}, "t2-park")])
    emit([{"header": header,
           "recall_diagnostic": diagnostic,
           "system": {"memory": {"bundle": {"text": json.dumps(bundle, sort_keys=True)}}},
           "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": "recall",
                         "text": "\n".join(lines)}]}])

# --------------------------------------------------- tier 2: the downgrade
if phase == "t2-downgrade" and op == "select" and not err:
    # The tier-1 bundle this request already rendered, read back as ONE row.
    # #418: it is DELIVERED, not rebuilt -- running the projection a second time
    # over a store that may have moved in the meantime is a second chance to
    # answer differently, and a downgrade that answers differently is not a
    # downgrade. The two marks are the ones this path has always carried.
    parked_rows, _worst = legs_from(rows_of(d))
    rendered = parked_rows.get("rendered")
    if not isinstance(rendered, dict) or not rendered.get("bundle"):
        # Nothing parked: the request never reached its own emission, so there
        # is no tier-1 answer to fall back to. Silence here is the one thing
        # #144 forbids, so it is said on stderr and the round closes.
        sys.stderr.write("recall: tier 2 failed and nothing was parked for %s\n" % rid)
        park()
    bundle = rendered["bundle"]
    bundle["tier_downgraded_from"] = 2
    header = {"route": "bundle", "recall_id": rid, "tier_downgraded": "1"}
    if query_hygiene is not None:
        header["query_hygiene"] = query_hygiene["step"]
    if not (bundle.get("candidates") or []):
        header["recall_empty"] = "1"
    emit([{"header": header,
           "recall_diagnostic": rendered.get("diagnostic") or {},
           "system": {"memory": {"bundle": {"text": json.dumps(bundle, sort_keys=True)}}},
           "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": "recall",
                         "text": "\n".join(rendered.get("lines") or [])}]}])

# ------------------------------------------------------- tier 2: the answer
if phase == "answer":
    finish = str(hop.get("finish_reason", ""))
    body = payload_of(d)
    text = ""
    for m in d.get("messages", []):
        if m.get("text"):
            text = m["text"]
            break
    if finish == "error":
        # Never silence: a provider error downgrades to the tier-1 bundle this
        # request already RENDERED, parked as ONE row rather than as the five
        # legs it was built from -- rebuilding it would mean running the
        # projection twice and hoping the two agree.
        emit([store_op({"operation": "select", "table": "recall_scratch",
                        "columns": ["request_id", "leg", "payload", "fired"],
                        "where": {"request_id": rid, "leg": "rendered"}},
                       "t2-downgrade")])
    parsed = body if isinstance(body, dict) else None
    if parsed is None:
        try:
            parsed = json.loads(re.sub(r"^```[a-z]*|```$", "", text.strip(), flags=re.M))
        except Exception:
            parsed = None
    gap_missing = False
    if not isinstance(parsed, dict):
        parsed = {"answer": text, "sources": [], "confidence": None}
        gap_missing = True
    gap = str(parsed.get("gap") or "").strip()
    if not gap:
        gap = "unavailable - the model returned no gap statement"
        gap_missing = True
    answer = {"query": query, "tier": 2, "as_of": as_of,
              "answer": str(parsed.get("answer") or ""), "gap": gap,
              "gap_missing": gap_missing,
              "sources": parsed.get("sources") or [],
              "confidence": parsed.get("confidence")}
    header = {"route": "bundle", "recall_id": rid}
    if gap_missing:
        header["gap_missing"] = "1"
    emit([{"header": header,
           "system": {"memory": {"answer": {"text": json.dumps(answer, sort_keys=True)}}},
           "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": "recall",
                         "text": "ANSWER: %s\nGAP: %s\nSOURCES: %s"
                                 % (answer["answer"], answer["gap"],
                                    ", ".join(str(s) for s in answer["sources"]))}]}])

park()
