tier0_max_episodes.description: Item cap of the bundle's episode leg. Since 3.13.3 (GH #1098) shipped as null: it grows with the asker's window by the factor the tier-0 budget grows by (12 at factor 1); a number overrides the package.

tier0_max_beliefs.description: Item cap of the bundle's belief leg, and the `limit` of the belief select behind it. Since 3.13.3 (GH #1098) shipped as null: it grows with the asker's window like `tier0_max_episodes` (20 at factor 1); a number overrides the package.

tier0_max_foresight.description: Item cap of the bundle's foresight leg (facts that are about a future the memory has been told about). Since 3.13.3 (GH #1098) shipped as null: it grows with the asker's window like `tier0_max_episodes` (10 at factor 1); a number overrides the package.

tier0_tokens.description: Token budget of the tier-0 bundle. Since 3.12.1 (GH #1085) shipped as null: it grows with the asker's window by the factor the tier-1 bundle grows by (1200 tokens at factor 1, 7500 for a 250k window); a request that names no window sizes it by `input_soft_fallback`; a number overrides both. An item has no length of its own: one that does not fit the bundle even alone is cut to what is left with the mark `...[cut: <shown> of <total> chars shown; budget of the window]`, and what the budget ended is named in the text (`...[dropped: <n> <list> over the bundle budget of <tokens> tokens]`) and in the JSON (`dropped`).

tier1_leg_limit.description: Per-leg candidate cap of the tier-1 fan. Since 3.10.0 (GH #1040) shipped as null: derived per request from the asker's model package (`recall_input_soft`, see `bundle_share`), 20 without a package; a number overrides the package.

tier1_axis_limit.description: Page bound of the AXIS reads — the hydration's chain select (`t1-hyd-axis`) **and** the window leg's generous pre-filter share it. Too small truncates a chain, and a candidate whose chain was cut is delivered **without its predecessors** — `history: []` on the record in `recall_diagnostic`, no `previously` key in the payload — rather than with a guessed chain

tier1_graph_nodes.description: `max_nodes` of the graph leg's `traverse` — the fan-out kill switch, so one hub entity cannot turn a recall into a walk of the whole graph

tier1_graph_fact_nodes.description: How many distinct walked nodes go into the join's `in` filter (GH #520). The walk is already ranked when the cut is taken, so what falls off is the tail of the walk, never its front

tier1_graph_fact_limit.description: Page bound of the join's `select facts` (GH #520). Generous on purpose: one popular subject carries a long version chain, and the leg's own `tier1_leg_limit` is the cut that decides what votes. A full page marks the leg **capped**, exactly as a full traverse page does

tier1_self_limit.description: Page bound of the **self** leg (GH #536): how many of the asker's own facts it NOMINATES, newest first. Generous, because a member's dossier is a small bounded set (21 live rows on the hive this was measured on) and the leg has no query signal to rank by: what it cannot rank it must not cut early. Since 3.10.0 (GH #1040) shipped as null: derived per request from the asker's model package like `tier1_leg_limit` (the question now ranks the page, but only the rows the page holds), 20 without a package; a number overrides the package

tier1_self_budget.description: How many of them may occupy a **bundle slot** while query-driven hits are waiting (GH #536). A different question from the one above: the leg nominates, the composition seats. Without it the dossier ate the fact half of every bundle — two different questions, one identical `FACTS` section. Leftover slots still fall back to the dossier, so it is a ceiling against competition and never a cut. Since 3.4.1 the budget counts **axes**, not rows ([#691](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/691)): the rows of one `(subject, predicate)` take one seat before any axis takes a second, and a multi axis (`has_child`) enumerates and is never folded. Since 3.10.0 (GH #1040) shipped as 0: no seat is reserved -- the self leg ranks its rows by the question, a matching row competes in the fused order and a row that matches nothing only fills places no ranked element wanted, so the dossier never displaces a better-ranked element; a number above 0 restores the reserved floor as an override

self_legacy_subject.description: The pre-canonicalisation spelling of *the member whose hive this is* (GH #536). The extraction lane writes a PERSON NAME into `facts.subject` today; everything written before it did carries the literal `user` — 23 of 29 self facts on the measured hive — and those rows are about the asker exactly as the new ones are. A **migration artefact**, named as one: the empty string switches it off for a hive that never had them. Since 3.10.0 (GH #1040) the rows it names are ranked by the question like every dossier row: one the question does not match fills only places no ranked element wanted, so the spelling displaces nothing and stays on until a hive has rewritten its subjects on the transfer lane

tier1_topk.description: How many fused candidates survive the RRF cut into the tier-1 bundle. Since 3.10.0 (GH #1040) shipped as null: derived per request from the asker's model package (`recall_input_soft`, see `bundle_share`), 20 without a package; a number overrides the package.

sem_max_distance.description: Relevance floor of the **semantic** leg (#297), as a fraction of the embedding's BIT WIDTH: a hit at or beyond `0.5 × dim` differing bits is where a random binary vector sits, so at the default the cut removes coin flips and cannot cost a genuine hit. `similar` RANKS and never filters — without this every one of its `tier1_leg_limit` rows votes in the fusion as loudly as a real hit. A missing, zero or non-numeric `dim` means no scale, and without a scale there is no cut

kw_min_score_ratio.description: Relevance floor of the **keyword** leg (#297), as a fraction of that page's OWN best bm25 rank — so the fact search and the episode search are never measured against each other's scale. bm25 is smaller-is-better, so the floor is `best × ratio` and a row survives at or below it. `0` switches the cut off (the ablation knob), and a page whose best rank is not negative carries no usable signal, so it is left uncut

bundle_episode_budget.description: The episode share of the fusion cut (P15 O-7): episodes take at most this many of the `TOPK` slots and keep that many against any fact wall. Whichever side cannot fill its share lets the other backfill, so the bundle is never shorter than a plain prefix would be. Since 3.10.0 (GH #1040) shipped as null: derived per request from the asker's model package (`recall_input_soft`, see `bundle_share`), 6 without a package; a number overrides the package.

tier1_tokens.description: Token budget of the tier-1 bundle; candidates are taken in fused order until the next one does not fit. It measures the **payload** candidate — what travels to the model — never the record in `recall_diagnostic`: the trace pays no prompt budget, so costing it would spend the whole #296 saving on refilling the budget instead of shipping a smaller bundle. `tier1_topk` stays the count cap. An item has no length of its own (GH #1085): one that does not fit the bundle even alone is cut to what is left with the mark `...[cut: <shown> of <total> chars shown; budget of the window]` and ends the list. Since 3.10.0 (GH #1040) shipped as null: derived per request from the asker's model package (`recall_input_soft`, see `bundle_share`), 2000 at factor 1; a request that names no window takes `bundle_share` of `input_soft_fallback` (GH #1085); a number overrides the package.

bundle_share.description: The share of the asker's usable window (its model package's `input_soft` -- the catalog row, cut by the curator to the model's own window alone since GH #1085 --, handed over as context `recall_input_soft` by the curator's ask, GH #1037/#1040) the tier-1 bundle may take, never less than 2000 tokens. Every count limit shipped as null (`tier1_topk`, `tier1_leg_limit`, `bundle_episode_budget`, `tier1_self_limit`) grows by the same factor, the three query limits by at most twice. An item has no length of its own (GH #1085): only the bundle counts. Context `input_soft` is read first, `recall_input_soft` is its alias. 0.05: luna's 250k soft limit, its catalog row for every role, gives a 12.5k-token bundle of 125 items, the low end of the 5-10 % KD2 proposed. Without a package every count and query limit keeps its old value, and the two bundles take their share of `input_soft_fallback` (GH #1085)

input_soft_fallback.description: The window in tokens of an asker no request names one for -- a tool caller without a curator, a peer, a harness (GH #1085, R-IG-1): such an asker has no born model this hive knows, so it is `input_soft` of the smallest chat row of the llm-registry catalog, the row `input_soft_fallback_row` names (OR-IG-9; a decisions or embeddings row never asks a memory). The tier-1 bundle takes `bundle_share` of it, never less than the old 2000 tokens, and the tier-0 bundle grows by the same factor; the count limits and the query guard stay at their old values (they select, and the curator mirrors the guard). With the shipped row (openai/gpt-4o-mini, 17500) the share is below 2000, so both bundles keep their old size. 0: no window, the bundles keep their old size.

input_soft_fallback_row.description: The catalogue row (`model_id` in `llm-registry/store/seed/models.jsonl`) whose `input_soft` `input_soft_fallback` is: an ask that names no window has no asker whose born model is known, so it is the smallest chat row of the catalogue (OR-IG-9, GH #1085). A label for the reader and for the drift lock `gh1085_fallback_windows_match_the_catalog`, which holds the two together; the script does not read it. A receiver born on another model sets both.

rrf_w_keyword.description: Fusion weight of the keyword (FTS) leg

rrf_w_semantic.description: Fusion weight of the semantic (embedding) leg

rrf_w_graph.description: Fusion weight of the graph (traverse) leg

rrf_w_temporal.description: Weight of the temporal leg **in window mode only** (P15 O-4)

rrf_w_self.description: Weight of the **self** leg (GH #536). Its rank list is recency, not relevance — it is the one leg the query does not shape — so a hit two query-driven legs agree on outranks it through the agreement factor rather than through a special case. `0` leaves the leg as discovery only, which is the ablation the eval prices

rrf_w_temporal_point.description: Weight of the temporal leg in **point** mode. Measured, not chosen: 50 identical LongMemEval extractions, paired — `0.0` gives R@1 **84.0 vs 74.0** and R@5 **98.0 vs 96.0**, flips **11:1** (sign test p=0.0063), and across 100 runs (2×50) the leg never carried a hit **alone**. Set it to `1.0` to restore the pre-O-4 fusion

rrf_agreement.description: Strength of the agreement factor in the fusion (#297): a candidate two VOTING legs found is multiplied once, three legs twice. `0` restores the plain rank sum

query_safe_chars.description: A query at or below this length reaches the legs untouched. Above it the hygiene guard runs (GH #88). Since 3.10.0 (GH #1040) shipped as null: derived per request from the asker's model package (`recall_input_soft`, see `bundle_share`), 200 without a package; a number overrides the package.

query_max_chars.description: Hard clamp of the hygiene guard: whatever survived the question / tail-sentence steps is cut to its last this many characters, so the cost of a recall stops depending on how much context the caller pasted. Since 3.10.0 (GH #1040) shipped as null: derived per request from the asker's model package (`recall_input_soft`, see `bundle_share`), 250 without a package; a number overrides the package.

query_tokens.description: How many tokens of the sanitised query reach the FTS matcher, taken from the TAIL — after the hygiene guard the tail is the question (GH #88). Since 3.10.0 (GH #1040) shipped as null: derived per request from the asker's model package (`recall_input_soft`, see `bundle_share`), 24 without a package; a number overrides the package.

tier1_graph_node_facts.description: GH #1057: at most this many facts of one walked node enter the graph leg -- first-hand facts before hearsay, then the ones that share a question word (names out), then the ones that share a value the best of them names, then newest first; for a question about now a value a newer first-hand value of the same axis replaced gets no seat, nor does a rumour where a first-hand fact answers, and a node the question does not name seats only facts its edge adds a question word to -- a node with fifteen facts cannot take every seat of the leg.

tier1_graph_fact_pages.description: GH #1057: the walked nodes (in walk rank, at most `tier1_graph_fact_nodes`) that get a fact page of their own; a walk that reached more reports `capped_at` with this number.

tier1_graph_node_page.description: GH #1057: the size of one walked node's fact page, newest first (at most `tier1_graph_fact_limit`); `rank_node_facts` chooses from it, and a full page reports `capped_at` with this number.

tier1_graph_anchors.description: GH #1057: the name anchors (question names first, then the names of the best keyword rows) the entity join looks up. Since 3.13.3 (GH #1098) shipped as null: it grows with the asker's window like `tier1_leg_limit` (96 at factor 1), a number overrides the package, and a cut is named in the bundle's `complete_reason`.

tier1_graph_start.description: GH #1057: the anchor entities the graph walk starts at, the ones the question names first. Since 3.13.3 (GH #1098) shipped as null: it grows with the asker's window like `tier1_leg_limit` (32 at factor 1), never past `tier1_graph_nodes` // (`tier1_graph_depth` + 1) -- the starts a page can walk from --, a number overrides the package, and a cut is named in the bundle's `complete_reason`.

stopwords_lang.description: The keyword leg's stop words as language DATA -- one block per language, `stopwords` a space-separated word list. Copied byte for byte from `recall/lang/<code>.json`; every language is applied at once. Absent or malformed, nothing is filtered.

recall_diagnostic.description: The retrieval's own record of the run -- the full candidate list, the readable ranking, the leg sizes before and after the floors. A top-level slot beside system/messages, so the collector's in_bundle lane drops it and it reaches the trace, never the next prompt (#296).

recall_empty.description: "1" when the bundle holds no candidate that answers the question -- absent otherwise, so a router can branch on the empty state without parsing the bundle (#297).

store_error.description: GH #343: the store's own `error_code` on a reply this lane refused to read as rows. It rides beside `reject_reason: "store_refused"` rather than inside it because the store's code list is OPEN (`invalid_input`, `query_timeout`, `write_denied`, `unknown_table`, `unknown_column`, `constraint_violation`, `sql_error`, ...), and an enum that has to grow with it would turn the next new code into a failed emit.

store_operation.description: GH #343: the op the store refused, as `hop.operation` named it -- `operation` says WHICH op answered, `error_code` says WHETHER it worked.

recall_subject.description: GH #948: the subject question as JSON text (`{subject, limit}`, the subject in the store's normal form) on `rsubj`. The store answers rows, not the question, so the edge carries it through the round trip in context.

subject.description: GH #948: a canonical subject (1..200 characters, matched in the store's normal form). Present, the request is a subject question: the newest facts of that subject under the asking round, no recall keys needed.

limit.description: GH #948: how many facts a subject question returns, 1..20 (default 10).

affect_filter.description: GH #936: the optional mark filter (a JSON object as text, promoted from `hop.affect_filter` by the hive's door): keys valence_max, valence_min, arousal_min, min_confidence. Applied AFTER the audience gate; a candidate without a mark falls out once it is set; a malformed one is refused at the request with `invalid_input`.

recall_subject.description: GH #948: the subject question, carried through the store round trip by the edge.

description.purpose: Tier-0 read path: asks the store ONCE for three fixed legs (recent episodes of the session, active beliefs of the holder, open foresight facts) -- one message carrying three tool_calls, one bundle reply carrying three results -- and emits ONE deterministic, token-budgeted bundle from that single hop (GH #295; no recall_scratch row is written for a tier-0 round). No LLM, no embedding, fixed latency. Since P3 the three legs filter, order and cap IN the store (as-of predicate for foresight), so the script never sees rows it would only drop.
description.use_when: Session boot and cheap ambient context; expose it as a recall tool lane. The caller promotes recall_query/memory_tier from hop to context on the port edge. The SAME edge must promote context.audience_now (a JSON list of participant ids in affinity vocabulary), context.channel and, where the room shows its history to whoever joins, context.channel_open_history='1' — without the first two the request is refused, not answered.
description.not_in_scope: No model in THIS cell: tier 0 is deterministic, tier 1 is an RRF fusion of legs the store computes (`search`, `similar`, `traverse`), and tier 2 asks ./dialectic and folds the answer back in -- the synthesis happens there, never here. Nothing is silently pretended either: a memory_tier this cell does not know, and a provider failure on the tier-2 leg, both DOWNGRADE and say so on hop.tier_downgraded='1'. And no write into the memory: the only table this cell inserts into or updates is its own recall_scratch fan-in.
description.emits_meaning: route rstore: the store ops of the current phase (hop.phase carries the state, hop.recall_id correlates the request; both are promoted to context by the edge). route bundle: the finished bundle — system.memory.bundle.text holds the machine-readable JSON, messages[] a readable tool_result. A tier-1/2 fact candidate of kind `foresight` carries `intent: planned` and renders as "… (planned)": since GH #67 a plan sits on the axis of the matter it is about rather than on a `plans_to_*` axis of its own, so the bundle is the place that has to keep an intention from reading as an accomplished fact. Incomplete fan-ins and lost guard races emit nothing (empty multi-send, terminal). route reject: a caller bug, never a silent default — hop.reject_reason names it ('missing_audience' when the query carries no participant set, 'missing_channel' when it names no room, 'half_open_window' when only one end of a window was given) and the tool_result says it in a sentence. A candidate (tier 1/2) or an open foresight item (tier 0) may carry `supersession_unknown: true` and render as "(currency unknown: cannot vouch that this still holds)": the audience gate removed a version from that axis, so the bundle states what it knows and refuses to assert that it is still in force. The flag is a boolean and carries nothing about what was removed — no count, no instant, no channel. GH #936: every candidate of the record carries `affect`, the mark of its source episode (null = unknown); the payload carries it where one exists. With `context.affect_filter` set, only candidates whose mark lies inside it remain -- after the audience gate, before the budget; the mark is never a ranking signal.
description.consumes_meaning: A message without a recall phase in context.mem_phase is a fresh request. Store replies are dispatched by (context.mem_phase, hop.operation); a tier-0 reply is the bundle of all three legs (mem_phase 'legs', hop.operation 'bundle', per-leg metadata in the body's results[] slot, correlated by tool_call_id), and in tier 1 hop.rows_affected on the guarded update decides who fires — exactly once per request per gate. hop.bundle_errors > 0 is a refused leg: tier 0 stops there on the reject lane rather than reading a poisoned bundle as rows. The python-side filters and sorts are kept as residual guards behind the store predicates: they are broader than SQL can express (e.g. '' counts as open, not just NULL) and make the migration result-identical by construction. AUDIENCE GATE (#244 / ADR-0002 E11): context.audience_now is the round that is asking, context.channel the room it asks from, context.channel_open_history (default '0') whether that room shows its history to whoever joins. A row with an EMPTY audience_set is refused first, before any other clause is reached (the open-history clause relaxes rows whose provenance is known, it never rescues a row whose provenance is missing). Otherwise a row is visible iff its audience_set contains '*', or the asking round is a SUBSET of it (the rule affinity/brief already decides disclosures with), or the row was recorded in THIS channel and the channel is open — the third clause never crosses a channel boundary, and a row without an audience_set is invisible, not visible. It is applied to candidates, not to rendered output: tier 0 gates each leg before the token budget is spent, tier 1 gates every leg before the RRF sum, so a hidden row can neither take a slot nor move the ranking of a visible one. episodes, facts and entity_edges carry channel + audience_set; a belief carries the set alone (it was derived, not said in a room, so the open-history clause cannot reach it). The semantic leg ranks embeddings, which are untagged, so the audience of the owning facts arrives as its own scratch leg (sem-aud) that the fan-in waits for. R7 (Nachtrag 3), the price of filtering first: the gate drops invisible versions BEFORE the version chain is built, because the other order would let the existence of an invisible version show through a validity span and let a persistent asker map out when something was said in a room they are not in. The price is that a claim whose successor is invisible would look current, so it is not paid silently — the surviving rows of a broken axis are marked in t1-hyd-axis (and in the tier-0 foresight leg), the mark becomes `supersession_unknown` on the candidate, the rendered line says so, and the dialectic prompt forbids presenting such a candidate as what holds now and requires the uncertainty in its gap statement. What the asker learns is only: I know this, and I cannot vouch that it still holds.
examples: {recall_query: 'what does alex drink', tier 0} -> ONE message with 3 tool_calls -> ONE bundle reply with 3 results -> bundle with beliefs/foresight/episodes
same request twice -> two independent recall_ids -> two byte-identical bundles

{audience_now: ["member:alex","agent:scribe"], channel: 'c1'} asking about something said in c1 before {member:alex, agent:scribe} -> answered; the same question with a third participant present -> the row is not in any leg at all

in_query without context.audience_now -> route reject, hop.reject_reason 'missing_audience'; without context.channel -> 'missing_channel' — never an empty bundle, which a caller cannot tell apart from 'memory knows nothing'

a fact superseded by a version this round may not see -> the bundle answers with the OLDER claim carrying supersession_unknown, not with the newer one and not with silence; the successor's claim, time and channel stay out of the bundle entirely
